Increase heat to medium-high. Add potatoes in an even layer; cook undisturbed 4 minutes, then toss and cook 6 to 8 minutes more until golden and crisp at edges.

Add onion and bell pepper with 1 tbsp oil if pan is dry; cook, stirring, until onion is translucent and peppers are tender, 4 to 5 minutes. Season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Fold in bacon.
Press hash into an even layer and cook 2 minutes to build crust. Taste and adjust seasoning. Reduce heat to medium-low and keep warm while frying eggs.

In a separate nonstick skillet, heat 1 tbsp oil over medium. Crack in eggs and cook sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks still runny, 3 to 4 minutes; or flip for over-easy, 30 to 60 seconds more.
Divide hash among 4 plates. Top each with a fried egg. Garnish with parsley and additional pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Breakfast Potatoes
steps: Before you do anything, freeze your bacon slices that way when you're ready to prep, it'll be so much easier to chop!
Wash the potatoes and cut medium dice into square pieces. To prevent any browning, place the already cut potatoes in a bowl filled with water.
In the meantime, heat 1-2 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Tilt the skillet so the oil spreads evenly.
Once the oil is hot, drain the potatoes and add to the skillet. Season with salt, pepper, and Old Bay as needed.
Cook for 10 minutes, stirring the potatoes often, until brown. If needed, add a tablespoon more of oil.
Chop up the bacon and add to the potatoes. The bacon will start to render and the fat will begin to further cook the potatoes. Toss it up a bit! The bacon will take 5-6 minutes to crisp.
Once the bacon is cooked, reduce the heat to medium-low, add the minced garlic and toss. Season once more. Add dried or fresh parsley. Control heat as needed.
Let the garlic cook until fragrant, about one minute.
Just before serving, drizzle over the maple syrup and toss. Let that cook another minute, giving the potatoes a caramelized effect.
Serve in a warm bowl with a sunny side up egg!

recipes.title: Brie wrapped in prosciutto & brioche
steps: Mix the flour, 1 tsp salt, caster sugar, yeast, milk and eggs together in a mixer using the dough attachment for 5 mins until the dough is smooth. Add the butter and mix for a further 4 mins on medium speed.
Scrape the dough bowl and mix again for 1 min. Place the dough in a container, cover with cling film and leave in the fridge for at least 6 hrs before using.

Wrap the Brie in the prosciutto and set aside. Turn out the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Roll into a 25cm circle. Place the wrapped Brie in the middle of the circle and fold the edges in neatly.
Put the parcel onto a baking tray lined with baking parchment and brush with beaten egg. Chill in the fridge for 30 mins, then brush again with beaten egg and chill for a further 30 mins.
Leave to rise for 1 hr at room temperature. Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, then bake for 22 mins. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Broccoli & Stilton soup
steps: Heat the rapeseed oil in a large saucepan and then add the onions. Cook on a medium heat until soft. Add a splash of water if the onions start to catch.
Add the celery, leek, potato and a knob of butter. Stir until melted, then cover with a lid. Allow to sweat for 5 minutes. Remove the lid.
Pour in the stock and add any chunky bits of broccoli stalk. Cook for 10 – 15 minutes until all the vegetables are soft.

Add the rest of the broccoli and cook for a further 5 minutes. Carefully transfer to a blender and blitz until smooth. Stir in the stilton, allowing a few lumps to remain. Season with black pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Brown Stew Chicken
steps: Squeeze lime over chicken and rub well. Drain off excess lime juice.
Combine tomato, scallion, onion, garlic, pepper, thyme, pimento and soy sauce in a large bowl with the chicken pieces. Cover and marinate at least one hour.
Heat oil in a dutch pot or large saucepan. Shake off the seasonings as you remove each piece of chicken from the marinade. Reserve the marinade for sauce.
Lightly brown the chicken a few pieces at a time in very hot oil. Place browned chicken pieces on a plate to rest while you brown the remaining pieces.
Drain off excess oil and return the chicken to the pan. Pour the marinade over the chicken and add the carrots. Stir and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Mix flour and coconut milk and add to stew, stirring constantly. Turn heat down to minimum and cook another 20 minutes or until tender.

recipes.title: Brun Lapskaus (Norwegian Beef Vegetable Stew)
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot. Cut beef into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes and brown in oil.
Dice the onion and add to browning beef. Add the stock and bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and let simmer for about 30 minutes.
Peel and cut the rutabaga and celery root into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes. Add to the pot, cover, and continue simmering for another 30 minutes.
Peel and chop the rest of the vegetables into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes and add to the pot. Slice the leek into rings. Cover and continue simmering for about 20 minutes. Stir as little as possible.
Top with fresh parsley.

recipes.title: Bruschetta al Pomodoro
ing: 1 lb ripe tomatoes, cored and finely diced
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, thinly sliced
1 loaf rustic Italian bread (about 12 oz), sliced 1/2-inch thick
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for brushing
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing
steps: Combine tomatoes, 1/4 cup olive oil, red wine vinegar, grated garlic, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper in a bowl; fold in basil. Let macerate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Preheat broiler to high or heat a grill to medium-high (about 450–500°F). Arrange bread slices on a sheet pan if broiling.
Brush both sides of bread with 2 tbsp olive oil. Broil or grill, turning once, until crisp at edges and well toasted with light char, 2–4 minutes total.
While hot, lightly rub one side of each slice with the cut side of the halved garlic clove.
Taste tomatoes and adjust seasoning with a pinch more salt or vinegar if needed. Spoon a generous mound onto each slice, letting juices soak in.
Finish with a light sprinkle of the finishing salt and drizzle 1 tbsp olive oil over the bruschette. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Bryndzové Halušky
steps: Prepare the Dough

Grate the potatoes finely using a hand grater or food processor. Place the grated potatoes in a bowl and mix them with flour, egg, and salt until a sticky dough forms. The consistency should be thick but pliable.
Cook the Dumplings

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Using a halušky maker (similar to a spaetzle maker), press the dough directly into the boiling water. If you don’t have one, use a tilted cutting board and a knife to scrape small pieces of dough into the water.
Let the dumplings cook until they float to the surface, usually within 2-3 minutes. Scoop them out with a slotted spoon and set aside in a large bowl.
Prepare the Toppings

Chop the bacon into small pieces and fry in a skillet over medium heat until crispy. If using a bryndza substitute, mix crumbled feta with a dollop of sour cream to mimic the tangy flavour of traditional Slovak sheep cheese.
Assemble the Dish

Toss the cooked dumplings with the bryndza cheese (or substitute) until they’re well-coated and creamy. Top with the crispy bacon and its drippings. Garnish with chopped chives or parsley for an extra touch of colour and flavour.

recipes.title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
ing: 1 1/4 lb peeled San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil over high heat. Salt the water with 1 tbsp kosher salt.
Set a wide skillet over medium heat. Add guanciale and 1 tsp frying oil if needed to start rendering. Cook, stirring, until golden and crisp, 7–9 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add red pepper flakes to the rendered fat and bloom 30 seconds. Raise heat to medium, pour in white wine, and simmer until mostly reduced, 2–3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Simmer gently over medium-low, stirring occasionally, until lightly thickened and glossy, 10–12 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
While the sauce simmers, cook bucatini in the boiling water until very al dente, 1–2 minutes shy of package time (about 7–8 minutes). Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add drained bucatini to the sauce with 1/2 cup reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously until the pasta is coated and the sauce clings, 1–2 minutes.
Off the heat, sprinkle most of the Pecorino Romano and toss until creamy, adding splashes of pasta water as needed for a silky emulsion.
Serve immediately, topped with remaining guanciale bits if separated in the pan and a final shower of Pecorino Romano.

recipes.title: Budino Di Ricotta
steps: Mash the ricotta and beat well with the egg yolks, stir in the flour, sugar, cinnamon, grated lemon rind and the rum and mix well. You can do this in a food processor.
Beat the egg whites until stiff, fold in and pour into a buttered and floured 25cm cake tin. Bake in the oven at 180ºC/160ºC fan/gas 4 for about 40 minutes, or until it is firm.
Serve hot or cold dusted with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
ing: 2 lb chicken wings, flats and drumettes separated, patted dry
1/2 cup Frank's RedHot Original cayenne pepper sauce
1/2 cup blue cheese dressing, for serving
steps: Adjust oven rack to upper-middle and heat to 450°F. Line a rimmed sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top; brush rack lightly with 1 tbsp frying oil.
In a bowl, toss wings with baking powder, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper until evenly coated. Arrange skin-side up on rack, spacing slightly.
Bake at 450°F for 35 to 45 minutes, rotating sheet halfway, until skin is deeply browned and crisp and wings reach 165°F internally.
Near the end of baking, melt 4 tbsp butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Whisk in 1/2 cup hot sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, and 1/4 tsp garlic powder; simmer for 1 minute, then remove from heat.
Transfer hot wings to a large bowl. Pour warm sauce over and toss until every piece is coated and glossy.
Rest sauced wings 2 minutes to set, then serve immediately with blue cheese dressing, celery, and carrot sticks.

recipes.title: Bulgarian Green Salad
steps: Place sliced lettuce in a large bowl.
Add radishes, cucumber, and scallions.
Drizzle with vinegar and olive oil.
Season with salt and gently toss to combine.
Top with sliced hard-boiled eggs, olives, dill and (or) parsley if using and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Bulgarian Honey Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 350 F. Line 2-3 baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a bowl, combine flour, salt, cinnamon and baking soda.
In the bowl of a stand mixer, fitted with the paddle attachment, beat together eggs and powdered sugar for3 minutes. Add vanilla extract and honey. Mix to combine, then add oil.
Add the flour mixture in two increments and beat to incorporate. Let the dough rest for 5-10 minutes.
Shape 2 tbsp balls, place on baking sheets and press flat. Bake for 12-15 minutes, until golden. Let the cookies cool down completely.
Melt white and semi-sweet chocolate separately with 1 tbsp vegetable oil each.
Dip cookies halfway into chocolate. Let it set. Keep in a air tight container or wrapped in cellophane bags for up to 2 weeks in room temperature or refrigerated.

recipes.title: Bulgogi
ing: 1 1/2 lb beef ribeye, very thinly sliced
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: In a bowl, whisk soy sauce, sugar, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, grated Asian pear, grated onion, garlic, ginger, and black pepper until sugar dissolves, about 1 minute.
Add sliced ribeye and massage to coat well. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes (up to 4 hours for deeper flavor).
Drain excess marinade well to encourage browning; reserve onions from marinade if desired.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or grill pan over high heat until smoking, about 3 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil and swirl to coat.
Working in batches to avoid crowding, spread beef in a single layer and sear, turning once, until browned and just cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes total per batch.
Add sliced onion, carrot, and scallions to the pan with the last batch and stir-fry until crisp-tender, about 1 to 2 minutes.
Return all cooked beef to the pan, toss with vegetables, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed; serve immediately.
Optional: For charcoal grill, preheat to high heat. Oil grates, then grill beef slices over direct heat, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until lightly charred and cooked through.

recipes.title: Burek
steps: Fry the finely chopped onions and minced meat in oil. Add the salt and pepper. Grease a round baking tray and put a layer of pastry in it. Cover with a thin layer of filling and cover this with another layer of filo pastry which must be well coated in oil.
Put another layer of filling and cover with pastry. When you have five or six layers, cover with filo pastry, bake at 200ºC/392ºF for half an hour and cut in quarters and serve.

recipes.title: Burrito Bowl
ing: 15 oz black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Combine 2 cups water and 1 tsp salt in a saucepan; add 1 cup rinsed rice. Bring to a boil, reduce to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Rest off heat, covered, 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
In a bowl, toss 1 lb sliced skirt steak with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, and 1/2 tsp smoked paprika.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp frying oil. Sear steak in a single layer until browned and just cooked through, 4–6 minutes total; remove to a plate and tent to keep warm.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add 1/2 cup diced onion and cook 2 minutes. Stir in 2 cloves minced garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add 15 oz rinsed black beans and 1 cup corn to the skillet with 2 tbsp water; simmer for 3–4 minutes until heated through. Stir in 1 tbsp lime juice; adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Prepare toppings: 1 cup pico de gallo, 1 cup shredded Monterey Jack, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup guacamole, and 1/4 cup chopped cilantro.
Assemble bowls: divide rice among 4 bowls, top with beans and corn, then steak and any juices. Add pico de gallo, cheese, sour cream, guacamole, and cilantro.
Serve immediately while warm; offer extra lime wedges if desired.

recipes.title: Butter Chicken
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Combine yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and salt; add chicken and coat well. Marinate 30 minutes at room temp or up to 8 hours chilled.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high. Shake excess marinade and sear chicken in two batches until lightly charred, 3–4 minutes per side; set aside. Chicken will finish cooking in sauce.
In the same pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium. Add tomato puree and sugar; cook, stirring, until thick and glossy, 6–8 minutes to reduce raw taste.
Stir in water and bring to a simmer. Add seared chicken and any juices; simmer gently over medium-low until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender, 8–10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in cream, remaining 1 tbsp butter, crushed fenugreek leaves, and black pepper. Simmer for 2 minutes; adjust salt and chili to taste.
Rest off heat 3 minutes for flavors to meld. Garnish with cilantro and a drizzle of cream. Serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Pancakes
ing: 3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled
1 tbsp frying oil or butter, as needed
1 cup berries or sliced fruit, for serving
steps: Whisk 2 cups flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, and 1/2 tsp salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk 2 cups cold buttermilk, 2 eggs, 3 tbsp melted butter, and 1 tsp vanilla until smooth.
Pour wet into dry; gently stir just until a few streaks of flour remain. Do not overmix; batter should be lumpy. Let rest 5 minutes.
Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium to medium-low until a drop of water skitters, about 375°F. Lightly grease with oil or butter.
Scoop 1/4 cup batter per pancake onto the griddle, spacing apart. Cook until edges set and bubbles break and stay open, 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook until golden and centers spring back, 1 to 2 minutes more. Keep finished pancakes warm at 200°F while repeating.
Regrease the pan as needed and adjust heat to maintain even browning without scorching.
Serve hot with maple syrup and fruit.

recipes.title: Bánh Mì Thịt
steps: Make quick pickle: combine 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1/3 cup water, 2 tbsp sugar, and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl; stir to dissolve. Add 1 cup carrots and 1 cup daikon; toss and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Marinate pork: mix 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tsp sesame oil, 2 cloves minced garlic, and 1 tsp black pepper. Add 1 lb thin-sliced pork; toss and marinate 20–30 minutes.
Sear pork: heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook pork in batches 5–7 minutes total until browned and juices run clear, 145°F; rest 5 minutes.
Warm rolls: heat oven to 350°F. Bake 4 banh mi rolls directly on rack for 5–7 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside; cool 2 minutes, then split lengthwise without cutting through.
Prepare spreads: mix 1/2 cup mayonnaise with a spoon to loosen. Have 2 tbsp pâté ready at room temperature for easy spreading.
Assemble: spread mayo on both cut sides of each roll; smear about 1/2 tbsp pâté per side. Layer warm pork along the bottom of each roll.
Add pickles and veg: drain carrot-daikon pickle well. Add cucumbers, a generous handful of pickles, cilantro sprigs, and jalapeño slices to each sandwich.
Finish and serve: press gently to compact. Serve immediately while bread is crisp and fillings are cool-warm contrasted.

recipes.title: Cabbage Soup (Shchi)
steps: Add the butter to a large Dutch oven or other heavy-duty pot over medium heat. When the butter has melted, add the onion and sauté until translucent.
Add the cabbage, carrot, and celery. Sauté until the vegetables begin to soften, stirring frequently, about 3 minutes.
Add the bay leaf and vegetable stock and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the vegetables are crisp-tender, about 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and bring it back to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, until the potatoes are tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes (or undrained canned tomatoes) and bring the soup back to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
emove and discard the bay leaf from the pot.
Serve topped with fresh sour cream and fresh dill.

recipes.title: Cabbage with Ground Beef
steps: Heat a large skillet or braiser over medium heat on the stovetop. Add the olive oil.
A braiser with cooked ground beef
Cook the Meat:
Add the ground meat to the pan. Use a potato masher or wooden spoon to break it into small pieces. Cook for 3–4 minutes until browned.
Add Vegetables and Seasoning:

Stir in the onion, carrots, red pepper, garlic, and tomato paste. Season with salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, ground cumin, and Italian seasoning (if using). Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring frequently.
A braiser with cooked ground beef, carrots, onions, peppers, garlic and seasoning.
Add Cabbage and Liquid:

Add the chopped cabbage, apple cider vinegar or lemon juice (if using), and water. Stir well to combine. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 30 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent the cabbage from sticking to the bottom of the pan.
A pot with cooked ground beef, vegetables and cabbage on a stove top
Check for Doneness:
Uncover and check the texture of the cabbage. If necessary, increase the heat to medium-high and cook for an additional 5–7 minutes to evaporate excess liquid and finish cooking.
A braiser with cooked ground meat and cabbage dish on a stove top
Garnish and Serve:
Sprinkle with chopped parsley or fresh herbs before serving.

recipes.title: Cacik
steps: Put a sieve over a large bowl, line it with a thick sheet of non-dyed kitchen paper or a clean muslin cloth, and spoon in the yogurt. Cover with another sheet of kitchen paper and leave to strain in the fridge for a minimum of 12 hrs.

Add the lemon juice, most of the olive oil and the dried mint to a bowl and stir well for the dried mint to soften and soak up the juices. Mix in the strained yogurt, then pour away the strained yogurt liquid and leave that bowl to one side.

Halve the cucumber(s) lengthways and remove the seeds by running a teaspoon from the top to the bottom of the flesh, halve the cucumbers widthways to make them shorter and easier to handle, then coarsely grate each one into the bowl the yogurt was straining over. Using clean hands (or a clean muslin cloth), squeeze as much of the liquid out of the cucumber as possible.
Add the strained, grated cucumber, garlic and ¾ tsp flaky salt to the rest of the ingredients and mix well. Garnish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of dried mint.

recipes.title: Cacio e Pepe
ing: 1/2 cup pasta cooking water, reserved hot
1 tbsp olive oil, as needed for pan
steps: Bring 3 quarts water to a rolling boil over high heat, season with 1 tsp kosher salt.
Toast 1 1/2 tsp black pepper with 1 tbsp olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat for 1 minute, then turn heat off.
Cook 12 oz spaghetti until just shy of al dente, 1 to 2 minutes less than package time; reserve 1 cup boiling water.
Add 1/2 cup reserved hot pasta water to the skillet, simmer 30 seconds over medium to bloom the pepper and form a peppery liquid.
Transfer spaghetti to the skillet; toss over medium heat until coated and some water is absorbed, about 1 minute.
Off the heat, vigorously toss while sprinkling in 1 1/4 cups Pecorino a little at a time, adding more hot pasta water by tablespoons to form a silky emulsion, 1 to 3 minutes.
Return to low heat only if needed, tossing constantly, to keep the sauce fluid; stop before it thickens too much. Season with more pepper if desired.
Serve immediately, twirling portions; the sauce should be glossy and cling in a thin, creamy layer.

recipes.title: CAFE LA LLAVE ESPRESSO ICE CREAM
steps: A note about the espresso: I like using the fine ground espresso brick and making the coffee in a regular moka pot, but you can certainly also use the Nespresso style capsules if you have that type of espresso maker. FULL DISCLOSURE: I personally prefer the decaf espresso, which the Cafe La Llave brand makes to perfection. The ice cream flavor holds either way.
In a medium saucepan, heat the cream, milk, sugar and salt over medium heat; whisking to dissolve the sugar (this should take about 4 to 5 minutes).
In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks.
Gradually pour about 1 cup of the hot milk mixture into the egg yolk bowl, while continually whisking. Do this carefully to temper the eggs. (You’re not cooking them.)
Add the tempered egg yolk mix back into the pan while whisking until it just comes to a simmer.
Remove the pan from the heat, then add the vanilla extract and espresso.
you can use any ice cream maker. It doesn’t have to be fancy.
Use between 2 and 4 shots of espresso (regular or decaf) depending on how strong you like the coffee flavor in the ice cream. I think about 3 shots is ideal.
This recipe will yield about 1 quart of ice cream.
Please sit back and enjoy your espresso ice cream. Also, stay cool. You’re welcome

recipes.title: Cajun spiced fish tacos
steps: Cooking in a cajun spice and cayenne pepper marinade makes this fish super succulent and flavoursome. Top with a zesty dressing and serve in a tortilla for a quick, fuss-free main that's delightfully summery.
On a large plate, mix the cajun spice and cayenne pepper with a little seasoning and use to coat the fish all over.

Heat a little oil in a frying pan, add in the fish and cook over a medium heat until golden. Reduce the heat and continue frying until the fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes. Cook in batches if you don’t have enough room in the pan.
Meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.

Soften the tortillas by heating in the microwave for 5-10 seconds. Pile high with the avocado, lettuce and spring onion, add a spoonful of salsa, top with large flakes of fish and drizzle over the dressing.

recipes.title: Caldo Verde
ing: 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and sliced 1/4 inch
8 oz collard greens, very thinly shredded
1 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, for garnish, as needed
steps: Warm 2 tbsp olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add chouriço and fry until edges render and brown, 3 to 4 minutes. Lift chouriço out and reserve; leave drippings in pot.
Add onion to the pot and cook until translucent, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant, without browning.
Add potatoes and stock. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 15 minutes until potatoes are very tender.
Mash most potatoes against the pot sides or use an immersion blender for 5 to 10 seconds to achieve a mostly smooth, lightly rustic texture.
Return the chouriço to the pot. Stir in collard greens, salt, and pepper. Simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes until greens are tender but bright.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Ladle into warm bowls, drizzle each with a little olive oil, and garnish with parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Callaloo and SaltFish
steps: Soak salted fish in water overnight. Next, heat salted fish in water on stove until water boils. You should see a foam on top. Remove from heat and drain. Set aside and shred salted fish once it cools.
Cook bacon in skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon from heat and drain the majority of the bacon grease, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the skillet.
Add yellow onion, green onion, scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic to the skillet and stir. Cook for about 2 minutes or until onions soften. Add salted fish to skillet and stir. Cook for about a minute.
Next, add callaloo, roma tomatoes, thyme, and black pepper. Stir to combine and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes.
Enjoy

recipes.title: Callaloo Jamaican Style
steps: Cut leaves and soft stems from the kale branches, them soak in a bowl of cold water for about 5-10 minutes or until finish with prep.
Proceed to slicing the onions, mincing the garlic and dicing the tomatoes. Set aside
Remove kale from water cut in chunks.
Place bacon on saucepan and cook until crispy. Then add onions, garlic, thyme, stir for about a minute or more
Add tomatoes; scotch bonnet pepper, smoked paprika. Sauté for about 2-3 more minutes.
Finally add vegetable, salt, mix well, and steamed for about 6-8 minutes or until leaves are tender. Add a tiny bit of water as needed. Adjust seasonings and turn off the heat.

Using a sharp knife cut both ends off the plantain. This will make it easy to grab the skin of the plantains. Slit a shallow line down the long seam of the plantain; peel only as deep as the peel. Remove plantain peel by pulling it back.
Slice the plantain into medium size lengthwise slices and set aside.
Coat a large frying pan with cooking oil spray. Spray the tops of the plantains with a generous layer of oil spray and sprinkle with salt, freshly ground pepper.
Let the plantains "fry" on medium heat, shaking the frying pan to redistribute them every few minutes.
As the plantains brown, continue to add more cooking oil spray, salt and pepper (if needed) until they have reached the desired color and texture.
Remove and serve with kale

recipes.title: Calzone
ing: 1 cup canned San Marzano tomatoes, crushed by hand
steps: Heat oven to 475°F with a preheated sheet or stone inside; allow 30 minutes for the stone to fully heat.
Stir tomatoes with olive oil, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, and 1/4 tsp salt; set aside. In a bowl mix mozzarella, ricotta, Pecorino, and black pepper until evenly combined.
Divide dough into 4 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each into an 8-inch round, about 1/8 inch thick.
Spread 2 tbsp tomato mixture on half of each round, leaving a 3/4-inch border. Top with one quarter of the cheese mix and prosciutto, keeping edges clean.
Fold dough over filling to form a half-moon. Press edges to seal, then crimp firmly. Poke a small steam vent on top with a knife tip.
Brush tops lightly with frying oil. Transfer calzoni to the hot stone or sheet and bake at 475°F for 14–16 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
If bottoms brown too fast, move to a higher rack and continue 2–3 minutes more. Let rest 5 minutes to allow cheese to set before serving.
Serve hot with remaining tomato sauce on the side for dipping.

recipes.title: Camaro Grelhado Com Molho Cru (Grilled Prawns with Green Onion Sauce)
steps: Make the sauce by combining all the ingredients and grinding them into a paste.
Put the prawns on the skewers and brush with sauce.
Grill until done (they should lose their translucent color), about 3-4 minutes on each side.
Serve with extra sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Cambodian Stir-fried Morning Glory with Pork, Fermented Soybeans, and Garlic
steps: In a wok or large pan, heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil over medium heat. Once the oil is hot, add the garlic and stir-fry for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not burnt.
Add the minced pork to the pan and break it up with a spatula. Stir-fry until the pork is fully cooked and browned, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the fermented soy beans and cook for another minute, mixing it thoroughly with the pork.
Toss in the cut morning glory and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes to retain its bright green colour and crisp texture.
Check the seasoning and adjust with fish sauce or sugar if needed. Transfer to a serving dish and serve immediately with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Cambodian Waffles (Num Poum)
steps: In a bowl, mix the flour, coconut milk, palm sugar and eggs and salt. Brush a waffle iron with oil pour in the batter and cook over an open fire until light brown and crispy.

recipes.title: Canadian Butter Tarts
steps: Preheat the oven to fan 170C/ conventional 190C/gas 5. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface so it’s slightly thinner than straight from the pack. Then cut out 18-20 rounds with a 7.5cm fluted cutter, re-rolling the trimmings. Use the rounds to line two deep 12-hole tart tins (not muffin tins). If you only have a regular-sized, 12-hole tart tin you will be able to make a few more slightly shallower tarts.

Beat the eggs in a large bowl and combine with the rest of the ingredients except the walnuts. Tip this mixture into a pan and stir continuously for 3-4 minutes until the butter melts, and the mixture bubbles and starts to thicken. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. Don’t overcook, and be sure to stir all the time as the mixture can easily burn. Remove from the heat and stir in the nuts.

Spoon the filling into the unbaked tart shells so it’s level with the pastry. Bake for 15-18 minutes until set and pale golden. Leave in the tin to cool for a few minutes before lifting out on to a wire rack. Serve warm or cold.

recipes.title: Caprese Salad
steps: Pat tomato and mozzarella slices dry with paper towels to reduce excess moisture.
On a platter, alternate tomato and mozzarella slices with whole basil leaves, slightly overlapping, forming a neat ring or rows.
Drizzle 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil evenly over the salad.
Sprinkle 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper evenly over the slices.
Optional: Drizzle 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar lightly over the tomatoes only to avoid masking the cheese.
Serve immediately at cool room temperature (68–72°F) for best flavor; do not chill once assembled.

recipes.title: Carbonada Criolla
steps: Brown the Beef: In a large pot, brown the beef cubes. Remove and set aside.
Sauté Vegetables: In the same pot, cook the onion until translucent. Add carrots, potatoes, and pumpkin, cooking for a few minutes.
Simmer: Return the beef to the pot. Add broth and dried apricots. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 1-2 hours, until the beef is tender.
Serve: Enjoy hot, with a crusty piece of bread.
Pro Tips:
Brown the beef in batches to ensure it gets a good sear, which adds depth to the stew's flavor.
Adding the fruits towards the end of cooking preserves their texture and adds a subtle sweetness to the dish.

recipes.title: Caribbean Tamarind balls
steps: Add tamarind pulp and 1 cup granulated sugar to a bowl and mash together with a spoon or fork. Take small amounts of the tamarind and sugar mix and shape them into small balls by rolling them in your hands. Make them the size of a marble or slightly bigger, as you like.
Add the remaining sugar to a flat surface, like a plate or a sheet pan. Roll the tamarind balls in granulated sugar until they're well-coated.
You can eat the tamarind balls immediately, or you can let them set for a few hours or overnight. Allowing them to set will give them a firmer texture and more crystallized sugar coating. Enjoy.

recipes.title: Carne Asada Tacos
steps: Whisk lime juice, orange juice, soy sauce, olive oil, cilantro, garlic, cumin, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl to make the marinade.
Pat steak dry, place in a shallow dish, and pour marinade over. Turn to coat. Marinate 20–30 minutes at room temperature (or up to 2 hours refrigerated; bring to room temp before cooking).
Heat a grill or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot, 3–5 minutes. Lightly oil grates or add a thin film of frying oil to the skillet just before cooking.

Shake excess marinade from steak. Sear over high heat until well browned and medium-rare, about 4–5 minutes per side (cook to 130–135°F for medium-rare or 140°F for medium). Rest on a board 5–10 minutes.
Warm corn tortillas on the grill or in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable and lightly charred, 30–45 seconds per side. Keep wrapped in a clean towel.
Slice steak thinly against the grain, then chop into bite-size pieces for easy tacos. Toss with any resting juices on the board.
Assemble tacos: fill warm tortillas with carne asada, top with white onion, cilantro, and salsa. Squeeze lime over to finish.
Serve immediately, with extra lime and salsa on the side.

recipes.title: Carnitas
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
1 lb pork belly, skin on, cut into 2-inch chunks
1/4 cup white onion, finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Combine pork shoulder and pork belly in a wide, heavy pot in a single layer. Add orange juice, milk, lard, water, salt, pepper, garlic, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, oregano, and onion slices.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low so liquid barely bubbles. Cover ajar and simmer for 75 minutes, turning meat every 20 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and increase heat to medium. Cook 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid evaporates and pork cooks in rendered fat.
Fry pork in its fat over medium-high heat 8–12 minutes, turning often, until edges are deeply browned and crisp. Remove cinnamon, bay leaves, and onion.
Check doneness: internal temp should reach 145°F for pork; rest 5 minutes. Break meat into large chunks with tongs; moisten with a spoon of rendered fat.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30–60 seconds per side until pliable.
Serve carnitas in tortillas with chopped onion, cilantro, and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Carrot and Bean Fritters
steps: Pour the beans into the sieve, remove liquid.
Grate carrots and add beans, Mix and mash together. Season with garlic, thyme, salt and pepper.
Form the dough into round buns, dip them slightly into the bread crumbs, and press the fritters.
Fry fritters in hot oil for a short time until the fritters are browned. Place on the greased or /baking paper-lined oven plate and bake at 200C for 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Carrot Cake
steps: For the carrot cake, preheat the oven to 160C/325F/Gas 3. Grease and line a 26cm/10in springform cake tin.
Mix all of the ingredients for the carrot cake, except the carrots and walnuts, together in a bowl until well combined. Stir in the carrots and walnuts.

Spoon the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. Remove the cake from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes, then carefully remove the cake from the tin and set aside to cool completely on a cooling rack.
Meanwhile, for the icing, beat the cream cheese, caster sugar and butter together in a bowl until fluffy. Spread the icing over the top of the cake with a palette knife.

recipes.title: Cashew Chicken
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut 3/4-inch
steps: Toss chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 1/4 tsp sugar; marinate 10 minutes while prepping vegetables and sauce.
Whisk sauce: 1 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin, sesame oil, chicken broth, and 2 tsp cornstarch until smooth; set by the stove.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat 2 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry chicken in a single layer until browned and cooked to 165°F, about 4–5 minutes; transfer to a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp oil to wok. Stir-fry onion and bell pepper until crisp-tender, about 2 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant.
Return chicken with any juices. Stir sauce, then pour in. Stir-fry until glossy and thickened, 1–2 minutes; if too thick, splash in 1–2 tbsp water.
Add cashews and scallions; toss 30 seconds. Season with white pepper and salt to taste. Remove from heat and serve immediately over steamed rice.

recipes.title: Cashew Ghoriba Biscuits
steps: Preheat the oven at 180 C / Gas 4. Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
In a bowl, mix the cashews and icing sugar. Add the egg yolks and orange blossom water and mix to a smooth homogeneous paste.
Take lumps of the cashew paste and shape into small balls. Roll the balls in icing sugar and transfer to the baking tray. Push an almond in the centre of each ghribia.
Bake until the biscuits are lightly golden, about 20 minutes. Keep an eye on them, they burn quickly.

recipes.title: Cassava bread
steps: Mix dry ingredients in a bowl
Add water and mix well
When mixture has achieved a doughy like consistency, roll into little balls
Roll balls with the palm of your hands, and flatten slightly like s disk
In a plate, cover balls with the rest of the farine to create a very course texture
Place on a hot heavy cast iron griddle pressing down to flatten with and roast on both sides until lightly brown
Remove and serve or add your special accompaniment

recipes.title: Cassava Cake
steps: Bring coconut milk to a boil. Add sugar, stirring until completely dissolved and continue to boil for about 45 minutes. Reserve ½ cup of the coconut milk/sugar mixture for later.
Combine remaining ingredients in a large mixing bowl, stir until well blended. Add hot coconut milk mixture and stir well. Mixture should be of a thick liquid texture.

Use 1 tablespoons of coconut milk mixture to grease baking pan. Pour batter into prepared baking pan and bake at 350°F (basting occasionally with reserved coconut milk mixture) for 2 to 3 hours or until knife inserted in centre comes out clean.
Spread any remaining coconut milk mixture over top of cake. Place cake on top of stove to cool completely.

recipes.title: Cassava pizza
steps: Preheat the oven to 200ºC.
Cut the bacon or chorizo into medium pieces and the paprika into strips.
Spread a little tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese on each portion of cassava.
Add the bacon or chorizo, corn, turkey ham, some olives and paprika.
Bake for 7 to 10 minutes.
Remove from the oven and enjoy.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Tacos
ing: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into small florets
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss cauliflower with frying oil, salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, and oregano until evenly coated.
Spread florets on a sheet pan in a single layer and roast at 425°F for 22 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned at the edges and tender.
Whisk sour cream, adobo sauce, lime zest, and lime juice in a small bowl; season crema with a pinch of salt to taste.
Warm corn tortillas directly over a burner or in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with roasted cauliflower, then top with onion, cilantro, and queso fresco.
Drizzle with chipotle-lime crema and serve immediately while hot.

recipes.title: Cayman Style Potato Salad
steps: Peel and cut potatoes in cubes, boil in salted water until tender. Chop peppers and onion and set aside. Mix together mayonnaise, mustard, sugar and black pepper and set aside.

Drain potatoes once tender and place in large mixing bowl. Add remaining ingredients and mix well. The salad may be served warm, but is normally served after it has been refrigerated for 2 to 3 hours.

recipes.title: Cayman-Style Lobster
steps: Rinse lobster under cold running water. Bring water and salt to boil in a 12 quart pot. Quickly plunge lobsters, headfirst, into boiling water. Cover and boil for 20 minutes or until lobsters turn red.

Remove lobster and allow it to cool. Remove lobster tails and cut shell down to middle to remove the meat. Cut the tail meat down the middle to remove the vein inside. Remove large claws and smaller legs by twisting them away from the body. A nut cracker can be used to crush the claw and legs to remove the meat inside.

Chop lobster meat. Heat butter or olive oil in large pan over low heat. Sauté red, green and scotch bonnet peppers, thyme and garlic. Add salt and chicken stock to pan. Then, add lobster meat and sauté for 10 to 15 minutes. Thicken sauce with the corn starch and water mixture.
Serve with your choice of vegetables, salad and/or rice.

recipes.title: Cevapi Sausages
steps: Place the ground meat in a bowl. Chop the onion very finely and grate the garlic cloves. Add to the bowl. Add the chopped parsley, all sorts of paprika, baking soda, dried breadcrumbs, water, Vegeta, salt, and pepper.
Mix well with the hand mixer fitted with the dough hooks. Cover the bowl with cling film/ plastic foil and leave to rest for 1 or 2 hours in the refrigerator.

Take portions of the meat mixture, about 50-55 g/ 1.7-1.9 oz/ ¼ cup portions, and form the cevapi. The rolls should be about as thick as your thumb and about 7-10 cm/ 3-4 inches long. I had 18 sausages. The recipe can be easily doubled.

Grill the cevapcici on the hot grill pan or on the barbecue for about 12-14 minutes, turning them several times in between, or until brown and cooked through. I checked by cutting one in the middle and then grilling the following batches for the same period of time.

Serve hot as suggested above. The cevapcici can be reheated in the oven at 180 degrees Celsius/ 350 degrees Fahrenheit for about 10 minutes or until heated through. Check one, if it is not hot enough, give the sausages a few more minutes.

recipes.title: Ceviche
ing: 1 lb firm white fish fillet, skinned and cut in 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup red onion, very thinly sliced
1 small ají limo or serrano chile, thinly sliced
1/2 cup cooked corn kernels or choclo, cooled
1 lime, cut into wedges for serving
steps: Rinse onion in cold water for 30 seconds, drain well, and pat dry to tame sharpness; set aside.
Chill a nonreactive bowl and the fish for 10 minutes to keep very cold. Pat fish dry and place in the chilled bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk lime juice, salt, pepper, and sugar until dissolved to make the leche de tigre.
Add fish and chile to the lime mixture, stir gently to coat, and marinate in the refrigerator for 10 to 12 minutes until fish turns opaque on edges.
Fold in the red onion and cilantro, toss gently, and rest 2 minutes to meld flavors.
Taste and adjust salt to balance bright acidity; the liquid should be vibrant and lightly seasoned.
Lightly oil 4 chilled plates with a few drops of frying oil, then divide ceviche and spoon over some leche de tigre.
Serve immediately with sweet potato slices, corn, and lime wedges; consume at once while cold.

recipes.title: Chakchouka
steps: In a large cast iron skillet or sauté pan with a lid, heat oil over medium high heat. Add the onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes, until softened. Add the peppers and garlic, and sauté for an additional 3-5 minutes.

Add the tomatoes, cumin, paprika, salt, and chili powder. Mix well and bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium low and continue to simmer, uncovered, 10-15 minutes until the mixture has thickened to your desired consistency. (Taste the sauce at this point and adjust for salt and spice, as desired.) Using the back of a spoon, make four craters in the mixture, large enough to hold an egg.
Crack one egg into each of the craters. Cover the skillet and simmer for 5-7 minutes, until the eggs have set. Serve immediately with crusty bread or pita.

recipes.title: Chakhokhbili
ing: 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in skinless, cut into large chunks
1/2 cup fresh basil (purple or sweet), chopped
1/2 cup water or low-sodium chicken stock
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high, add chicken in a single layer, and brown 4 to 5 minutes per side; work in batches and add oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium, add sliced onion to the pot drippings, and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic, ground coriander, paprika, and chili flakes; cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and any juices; scrape up browned bits.
Return chicken to the pot with 1/2 cup water or stock. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring once.
Uncover and continue to simmer until chicken is tender and sauce thickens and glistens, about 10 to 15 minutes; adjust salt and pepper. Ensure chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in most of the cilantro, parsley, and basil, reserving a little for garnish; simmer 2 minutes to meld flavors, then remove from heat.
Rest 5 minutes. Garnish with remaining herbs and serve hot with flatbread or rice.

recipes.title: Challah
steps: Combine the yeast, a pinch of the sugar and a couple tablespoons of lukewarm water in a small bowl. Stir to dissolve the yeast, then leave for 10 mins until foamy.

Meanwhile, combine the flour, the remaining sugar and 2 tsp fine salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the centre, then add half the beaten egg, the yeast mixture and the oil. Pour in 200ml lukewarm water (it should feel slightly warm to the touch) and stir with a spoon, then mix using one hand, keeping the other clean while you bring the dough together. If there are a lot of very dry bits, gradually add a little water to just bring it together – you don't want it to get too wet and sticky. The dough should be moist, but not soggy.

Once the dough has come together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead using both hands for 10 mins until smooth and a bit springy. If it gets very sticky, add a very small amount of flour – as little as possible. A dough scraper is useful if the dough is sticking to the work surface. Stretch the sides of the dough down and pull together to form a ball. Lightly oil a bowl, then lightly roll the dough ball around the bowl so it's coated in the oil. Cover with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm place for 1 hr, or until dough has doubled in size.

Line a baking sheet with baking parchment. Turn the dough out onto a clean work surface and divide into three equal pieces, weighing for accuracy, if you like. Roll each piece into a long sausage shape about 25cm long, tapering them slightly at both ends. Lay the pieces out in front of you, parallel to one another with a couple centimetres between each. Bring the sausages together at the top end, then plait them down the length, tucking in the ends when you reach the bottom. Carefully transfer the loaf to the prepared baking sheet and loosely cover with a clean tea towel. Leave to rise until puffy and billowy, about 40 mins.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Gently brush the rest of the beaten egg all over the challah, getting it into all the crevices, and sprinkle with the poppy or sesame seeds, if using. Bake on a middle shelf of the oven for 25-30 mins, until the loaf is golden brown underneath and sounds hollow when tapped. Check after about 15 mins – if the top of the loaf has started to get too dark, cover it with foil. Leave to cool on a wire rack, then serve.

recipes.title: Chana Masala
ing: 1/2 cup chickpea cooking liquid or water
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat for 1 minute. Add 1 tsp cumin seeds and toast until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until deep golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes. Add ginger and garlic; sauté until raw smell fades, 1 minute.
Stir in tomatoes; cook down until jammy and oil separates at edges, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add coriander, turmeric, Kashmiri chili, and 1/2 tsp salt; cook spices in the tomato base for 1 minute, stirring.
Add chickpeas and 1/2 cup chickpea liquid or water; bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Lightly mash a few chickpeas with the back of a spoon to thicken; simmer 3 more minutes to desired gravy consistency.
Stir in garam masala, amchur, and lemon juice; simmer 1 minute, then taste and adjust salt to taste.
Turn off heat, rest 2 minutes, then garnish with chopped cilantro and serve hot with rice or bhatura.

recipes.title: Char Siu
ing: 2 lb pork shoulder, cut into 3 long strips
steps: Whisk maltose, 2 tbsp honey, sugar, light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, five-spice, sesame oil, salt, white pepper, garlic, and food coloring (optional) until smooth.
Trim excess surface fat from pork. Add pork strips to marinade, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 8 to 24 hours, turning once halfway.
Remove pork 30 minutes before roasting. Heat oven to 425°F. Line a rimmed sheet with foil and set a rack on top; lightly oil the rack.
Arrange pork on rack, reserving marinade. Roast at 425°F for 15 minutes, then baste with marinade.
Reduce oven to 375°F. Continue roasting 20 to 25 minutes, basting every 7 to 8 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F internal.
Simmer remaining marinade in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes to reduce. Off heat, stir in remaining 2 tbsp honey to make glaze.
Brush pork all over with warm glaze and return to oven 3 minutes to set. Rest 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1/4-inch pieces.
Optional finish: briefly char edges under the broiler on high for 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, then re-glaze lightly before serving.

recipes.title: Cheese Borek
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk together egg, parsley, garlic and crushed red pepper. Mix in Gouda and Emmentaler.

One sheet at a time, place phyllo dough on a flat surface and brush with about 1 tablespoon butter. Cut lengthwise into 4 strips. Place a rounded teaspoon of the egg mixture at one end of each strip. Fold corner of strip over the filling, forming a triangular fold. Continue folding the length of the strip in triangular folds to form a small stuffed triangle. Repeat with remaining phyllo dough.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly butter a large baking sheet.
Arrange stuffed phyllo triangles in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven 30 minutes, or until lightly browned. Serve warm

recipes.title: Cheese Sticks
steps: Cut the cheese and long strips and place in your fridge to prevent it becoming soft. Mix flour, butter and egg in a bowl, and add sugar, salt and olive oil to taste into the mix.

Then gradually add milk and knead well for a suitable consistency. Stretch out the dough with a rolling pin and cut into long strips (2 to 3 cm) and then roll the strips of dough around the cheese strips forming a spiral.
Make sure the dough covers the cheese fully so that it doesn't melt out while frying. Roll the cheese & dough strips through flour to prevent them from sticking while frying.
Heat oil in a frying pan until hot before placing the cheese sticks, and fry until golden in color.

recipes.title: Chelsea Buns
steps: Sift the flour and salt into a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and add the yeast.
Meanwhile, warm the milk and butter in a saucepan until the butter melts and the mixture is lukewarm.
Add the milk mixture and egg to the flour mixture and stir until the contents of the bowl come together as a soft dough. (You may need to add a little extra flour.)
Tip the dough onto a generously floured work surface. Knead for five minutes, adding more flour if necessary, until the dough is smooth and elastic and no longer feels sticky.

Lightly oil a bowl with a little of the vegetable oil. Place the dough into the bowl and turn until it is covered in the oil. Cover the bowl with cling film and set aside in a warm place for one hour, or until the dough has doubled in size.
Lightly grease a baking tray.

For the filling, knock the dough back to its original size and turn out onto a lightly floured work surface. Roll the dough out into a rectangle 0.5cm/¼in thick. Brush all over with the melted butter, then sprinkle over the brown sugar, cinnamon and dried fruit.

Roll the dough up into a tight cylinder , cut ten 4cm/1½in slice and place them onto a lightly greased baking sheet, leaving a little space between each slice. Cover with a tea towel and set aside to rise for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 190C/375F/Gas 5.
Bake the buns in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until risen and golden-brown.
Meanwhile, for the glaze, heat the milk and sugar in a saucepan until boiling. Reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Remove the buns from the oven and brush with the glaze, then set aside to cool on a wire rack.

recipes.title: Chick-Fil-A Sandwich
steps: Wrap the chicken loosely between plastic wrap and pound gently with the flat side of a meat tenderizer until about 1/2 inch thick all around.
Cut into two pieces, as even as possible.
Marinate in the pickle juice for 30 minutes to one hour (add a teaspoon of Tabasco sauce now for a spicy sandwich).
Beat the egg with the milk in a bowl.
Combine the flour, sugar, and spices in another bowl.
Dip the chicken pieces each into the egg on both sides, then coat in flour on both sides.
Heat the oil in a skillet (1/2 inch deep) to about 345-350.
Fry each cutlet for 2 minutes on each side, or until golden and cooked through.
Blot on paper and serve on toasted buns with pickle slices.

recipes.title: Chicken & chorizo rice pot
steps: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish and brown the chicken pieces on all sides – you may have to do this in batches. Remove from the dish and put to one side.

Lower the heat, add the onion and pepper, and gently cook for 10 mins until softened. Add the garlic and chorizo, and cook for a further 2 mins until the chorizo has released some of its oils into the dish. Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 1 min more.
Return the chicken pieces to the dish along with the thyme, white wine and stock. Bring the liquid to a boil, cover the dish with a tight-fitting lid and lower the heat. Cook for 30 mins.

Tip in the rice and stir everything together. Cover, set over a low heat and cook for a further 15 mins, or until the rice is cooked and has absorbed most of the cooking liquid. Remove from the heat and leave the dish to sit for 10 mins to absorb any remaining liquid. Season to taste and scatter with parsley to serve.

recipes.title: Chicken & mushroom Hotpot
steps: Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Put the butter in a medium-size saucepan and place over a medium heat. Add the onion and leave to cook for 5 mins, stirring occasionally. Add the mushrooms to the saucepan with the onions.

Once the onion and mushrooms are almost cooked, stir in the flour – this will make a thick paste called a roux. If you are using a stock cube, crumble the cube into the roux now and stir well. Put the roux over a low heat and stir continuously for 2 mins – this will cook the flour and stop the sauce from having a floury taste.

Take the roux off the heat. Slowly add the fresh stock, if using, or pour in 500ml water if you’ve used a stock cube, stirring all the time. Once all the liquid has been added, season with pepper, a pinch of nutmeg and mustard powder. Put the saucepan back onto a medium heat and slowly bring it to the boil, stirring all the time. Once the sauce has thickened, place on a very low heat. Add the cooked chicken and vegetables to the sauce and stir well. Grease a medium-size ovenproof pie dish with a little butter and pour in the chicken and mushroom filling.
Carefully lay the potatoes on top of the hot-pot filling, overlapping them slightly, almost like a pie top.
Brush the potatoes with a little melted butter and cook in the oven for about 35 mins. The hot-pot is ready once the potatoes are cooked and golden brown.

recipes.title: Chicken 65
ing: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp vinegar, white or apple cider
steps: In a bowl, mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, pepper, cumin, coriander, turmeric, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, lemon juice, soy sauce, and vinegar to form a thick marinade.
Add chicken pieces, coat thoroughly, and rest for 20 minutes at room temperature (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat 1 1/2 inches frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches 4–5 minutes until deep red and cooked through to 165°F internal; drain on a rack.
Pour off most frying oil, leaving 2 tbsp in the pan. Heat over medium, add mustard seeds; let them splutter for 20 seconds.
Add curry leaves and slit green chilies; sauté 30–40 seconds until fragrant.
Sprinkle in sugar and add 2 tbsp water to create a light glaze; toss to combine for 20 seconds.
Add fried chicken to the pan; toss over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes to coat evenly and re-crisp.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges; rest 2 minutes before serving to set the crust.

recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
ing: 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup cooked jasmine rice, for serving, as needed
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish, as needed
steps: Pat chicken dry. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high until shimmering. Brown chicken skin-side down until deep golden, 6–8 minutes; flip and brown 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat. Add smashed garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce, cane vinegar, water, brown sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves; scrape up browned bits.
Return chicken skin-side up. Bring to a boil over medium-high, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Uncover, flip chicken, and simmer uncovered until tender and sauce reduces slightly, 10–12 minutes.
Flip chicken skin-side up. Increase heat to medium-high and simmer to glaze and thicken the sauce to a syrupy consistency, 5–7 minutes. Skim excess fat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Check doneness: chicken should reach 165°F at the thickest part. Remove bay leaves.
Serve chicken and spoon glossy adobo sauce over hot jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced scallions if desired.

recipes.title: Chicken Alfredo Primavera
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season both sides of each chicken breast with seasoned salt and a pinch of pepper.
Add the chicken to the skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes on each side, or until cooked through. While the chicken is cooking, bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Season the boiling water with a few generous pinches of kosher salt. Add the pasta and give it a stir. Cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 12 minutes.

Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water before draining the pasta. Remove the chicken from the pan and transfer it to a cutting board; allow it to rest. Turn the heat down to medium and dd the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter and olive oil to the same pan you used to cook the chicken.
Add the veggies (minus the garlic) and red pepper flakes to the pan and stir to coat with the oil and butter (refrain from seasoning with salt until the veggies are finished browning).
Cook, stirring often, until the veggies are tender, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and a generous pinch of salt and pepper to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze the pan with the white wine. Continue to cook until the wine has reduced by half, about 3 minutes. Stir in the milk, heavy cream, and reserved pasta water.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil and allow to simmer and reduce for 2-3 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the Parmesan cheese and cooked pasta. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Garnish with Parmesan cheese and chopped parsley, if desired.

recipes.title: Chicken and Dumplings
ing: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, add chicken skin-side down, and brown 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate; discard all but 1 tbsp fat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook over medium heat until softened, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Pour in chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Return chicken (and juices) to pot, skin removed if desired. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes until chicken reaches 175°F and is very tender.

Transfer chicken to a board; when cool enough, discard skin and bones and shred meat. Keep soup at a low simmer. In a small skillet melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat, whisk in 2 tbsp flour, and cook 1 minute to make a blond roux; whisk roux into the simmering broth to slightly thicken.
Make dumpling dough: In a bowl whisk 1.5 cups flour, baking powder, and 3/4 tsp salt. Cut in 3 tbsp cold butter until crumbly. Stir in milk just until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not overmix.
Return shredded chicken to the pot and taste; season broth with salt and pepper. Maintain a gentle simmer. Using a tablespoon, drop golf-ball-size mounds of dough onto the surface, spacing slightly.
Cover the pot tightly and simmer without lifting the lid for 15 minutes. Dumplings are done when puffed and cooked through (center reaches 200°F or a toothpick comes out clean).
Turn off heat, rest 5 minutes. Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Chicken and Potato Roti
steps: Add a pint of chicken stock to the simmer and put three tablespoons of sugar into a large saucepan on high; cook until the sugar caramelizes, then add the cubed chicken breasts and stir until the chicken browns.
Add chopped onions, garlic, parsley, thyme, jerk seasoning, salt, and the whole scotch bonnet pepper – do not cut up the pepper! Reduce the heat to low and let this simmer for 25 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, sift the flour, and add a pinch of salt to taste.
Now add the first tablespoon of shortening, and with your fingers, rub the flour into the shortening until it forms a breadcrumb-like consistency.
Then add the second tablespoon of shortening and rub against the flour until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Now add the third tablespoon of shortening and repeat the process.
You should by now have used all the flour. Your bowl should be all breadcrumb-like; if you still have fresh flour, use another tablespoon of shortening until your fresh flour is all used up.
Add a small amount of water and mix with a butter knife; keep adding small amounts until your mixture forms a soft dough.
Now dust your surface with flour and roll out your pastry; you want to roll wafer-thin rounds – this mixture should make at least 12 roti skins.
Cover with a tea towel while returning to the pot.
Now peel the potatoes and cube them into small bite-size pieces.
After 25 minutes of simmering, add 1/2 pint of water and the potatoes to the pool.
Now cover and cook for 30 minutes on low heat.
Turn a flat baking tray upside down, lightly cover with foil, and place on the stovetop on high; cook each roti skin for 1 minute on each side until brown but not crisp.
Now pile up your cooked roti skins, remove the pot after 30 minutes, and remove the whole scotch bonnet.

Take the entire pot to the table with a pile of plates; each person assumes the roti skin, lays it flat on the scale, spoons some filling into the middle of the roti skin, and folds around the filling eats enjoy.

recipes.title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 1-inch pieces
8 oz andouille sausage, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/4-inch thick
1 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
2 cups cooked white rice, warm, for serving
steps: Brown sausage in a large heavy pot over medium heat until well browned, 5 to 7 minutes; transfer to a plate, leaving drippings. Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper, brown in drippings 6 to 8 minutes; transfer.
Make a dark roux: add vegetable oil and flour to the pot. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly with a flat wooden spoon, until chocolate-brown, 25 to 35 minutes. Do not let it burn.
Stir in onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened and fragrant, 6 to 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until aromatic.
Whisk in chicken stock gradually until smooth. Add thyme, bay leaf, cayenne, browned sausage, and chicken with any juices. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered, skimming fat, until chicken is tender and flavors meld, 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust salt, black pepper, and cayenne. Remove bay leaf. If desired, skim more fat. Gumbo should be slightly thick; simmer longer to reduce or add a splash of stock to loosen.
Serve gumbo hot over warm cooked white rice. Garnish with scallions and parsley. Ensure chicken pieces reach 165°F internal temperature before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken and Waffles
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 8 pieces
1/4 cup maple syrup, plus more for serving
steps: Marinate chicken: In a bowl, whisk 1 cup buttermilk with 1 tsp hot sauce. Add chicken, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes while you heat oil and make waffle batter.
Heat oil: Pour frying oil 1 to 1 1/2 inches deep in a heavy skillet or Dutch oven. Heat to 350°F over medium heat; maintain 325–350°F during frying.

Make waffle batter: Whisk 1 3/4 cups milk, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 eggs, and 1/4 cup melted butter. In another bowl whisk 2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, and 1/2 tsp salt. Fold dry into wet just until combined.
Cook waffles: Preheat waffle iron. Lightly oil it, then cook batter in batches until golden and crisp, about 4–5 minutes per waffle. Hold finished waffles on a rack in a 200°F oven.

Dredge chicken: Mix 1 1/4 cups flour, 1/4 cup cornstarch, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Lift chicken from buttermilk, let excess drip, then coat thoroughly in dredge.
Fry chicken: Fry coated chicken in batches at 325–350°F until deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 165°F, about 5–7 minutes per batch. Drain on a rack; rest 3 minutes.
Serve: Place waffles on plates, top with fried chicken, and drizzle each serving with about 1 tbsp maple syrup. Offer extra warm maple syrup alongside.

recipes.title: Chicken Basquaise
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C/Gas mark 4. Have the chicken joints ready to cook. Heat the butter and 3 tbsp olive oil in a flameproof casserole or large frying pan. Brown the chicken pieces in batches on both sides, seasoning them with salt and pepper as you go. Don't crowd the pan - fry the chicken in small batches, removing the pieces to kitchen paper as they are done.

Add a little more olive oil to the casserole and fry the onions over a medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened but not browned. Add the rest of the oil, then the peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.

Add the chorizo, sun-dried tomatoes and garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes. Add the rice, stirring to ensure it is well coated in the oil. Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, bay leaves and chopped thyme. Pour in the stock and wine. When the liquid starts to bubble, turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. Press the rice down into the liquid if it isn't already submerged and place the chicken on top. Add the lemon wedges and olives around the chicken.

Cover and cook in the oven for 50 minutes. The rice should be cooked but still have some bite, and the chicken should have juices that run clear when pierced in the thickest part with a knife. If not, cook for another 5 minutes and check again.

recipes.title: Chicken Bastilla
ing: 1 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
1 lb bone-in chicken drumsticks, skin removed
1 cup whole almonds, toasted, roughly chopped
steps: Pat chicken dry and season with 1/2 tsp salt and black pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high, brown chicken 6 to 8 minutes, turning until golden.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, 1 tsp cinnamon, saffron, and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Stir, cover, and cook over medium-low until chicken is tender, 30 to 35 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Transfer chicken to a plate. Boil the sauce over medium to reduce to a thick jammy mixture, 6 to 8 minutes. Off heat, stir in cilantro and parsley.

When cool enough, remove chicken skin and bones, shred meat finely. Return pot to low heat, add beaten eggs to the onion mixture, and stir constantly until softly set and moist, 3 to 4 minutes. Cool completely.
Mix almonds with 1/4 cup sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon; set aside. Heat oven to 375°F. Brush a 9-inch pie pan with melted butter.

Layer 4 phyllo sheets in the pan, one at a time, brushing each with butter and rotating so edges overhang evenly. Spread half the almond mixture, then all shredded chicken, then the egg-onion mixture, then remaining almonds.
Fold phyllo over filling to enclose. Top with 4 more buttered phyllo sheets, tucking edges down the sides. Brush top with remaining butter and slash a few vents.
Bake at 375°F until deep golden and crisp, 28 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon before slicing and serving warm.

recipes.title: Chicken Biryani
ing: 1 1/2 lb bone-in chicken pieces, skin removed
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
1 tbsp whole spices (6 green cardamom, 6 cloves, 1 bay leaf, 1-inch cinnamon)
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1/4 cup warm milk, with a pinch of saffron
steps: Marinate: In a bowl combine yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, crushed fried onions, mint, cilantro, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, 2 tsp salt, and lemon juice. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Parboil rice: Bring 10 cups water to a rolling boil with 1 1/2 tsp salt, whole spices, and cumin. Add soaked rice and boil until 70% cooked, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain immediately and spread to steam-dry for 2 minutes.

Sear aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil in a heavy 4- to 5-qt pot over medium-high. Add marinated chicken in a single layer; cook 3 minutes per side to lightly sear, do not fully cook. Remove pot from heat.

Layer: Return chicken to pot in an even layer with all its marinade. Top with half the parboiled rice, sprinkle half the saffron milk and half the fried onions. Add remaining rice, saffron milk, and 1 tbsp ghee. Dot with 1 tbsp oil if dry.
Seal for dum: Cover the pot with a tight lid. For a loose lid, seal rim with a simple flour-water dough rope or wrap lid with foil to trap steam.
Steam (dum): Set pot over the lowest burner heat. Cook for 25 minutes until steam escapes steadily and internal chicken temperature reaches 165°F. Rest off heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
Finish: Gently fluff from the edges, lifting rice without breaking grains and turning pieces to coat in juices. Discard whole spices as found.
Serve: Plate biryani with a scatter of cilantro and reserved fried onions. Offer raita and lemon wedges alongside.

recipes.title: Chicken Cacciatore
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide heavy skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then brown chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.

Lower heat to medium. Add onion and bell pepper; cook, stirring, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook until they release liquid and begin to brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in sliced garlic for 30 seconds.
Deglaze with 1/2 cup white wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes until mostly reduced.
Stir in 1 cup crushed tomatoes, 1/2 cup chicken broth, capers, rosemary, and thyme. Return chicken skin-side up, nestling in sauce; bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, then uncover and continue to simmer until chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part, 10 to 15 minutes more.
Discard herb sprigs. Stir in olives and 1 tbsp red wine vinegar; simmer 2 minutes. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 5 minutes to settle flavors. Sprinkle with 2 tbsp chopped parsley and serve with polenta or crusty bread.

recipes.title: Chicken Caesar Salad
ing: 1 cup crusty bread, cut into 1-inch cubes
steps: Heat a skillet over medium; rub chicken with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Cook 5-7 minutes per side to 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Toss bread cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and minced garlic. Toast on a sheet pan at 375°F for 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until golden. Cool.
In a bowl, whisk grated Parmesan, egg yolk, lemon juice, Dijon, and anchovies until smooth, 30 seconds.
While whisking constantly, stream in 1/2 cup olive oil to form a creamy, emulsified dressing. Season with 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Place chopped romaine in a large bowl. Add enough dressing to coat leaves lightly; toss thoroughly, 30 seconds.
Add warm croutons and sliced chicken; toss again, adding more dressing as needed to lightly cloak everything.
Plate salad. Top with shaved Parmesan and a few extra cracks of black pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Chilaquiles
ing: 12 oz corn tortillas, cut into wedges
steps: Poach chicken: Bring 4 cups chicken broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat, add 1/2 tsp salt if broth is unsalted, slide in 1 lb chicken breasts, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until 165°F. Transfer to a plate to cool.

Make salsa verde: Simmer tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, and garlic in the poaching broth for 6–8 minutes until tomatillos pale and soften. Scoop solids to a blender with 1/2 cup cilantro and 1 tsp kosher salt; blend smooth.
Reduce salsa: Pour blended salsa into a skillet and simmer over medium heat for 5–7 minutes until slightly thickened and bright. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Shred chicken: Shred the cooled chicken into bite-size pieces and keep warm; moisten with a few spoonfuls of salsa to prevent drying.
Fry tortillas: Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet to 350°F. Fry tortilla wedges in batches for 2–3 minutes until crisp and lightly golden. Drain on paper towels and lightly salt.
Coat chips: Bring salsa to a lively simmer, add half the chips, toss gently to coat, then add remaining chips and shredded chicken. Cook 1–2 minutes, just until chips soften at edges but stay sturdy.
Finish and serve: Divide onto 4 plates. Top with Mexican crema, queso fresco, thin onion, avocado, and chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.

recipes.title: Chicken Chow Mein
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
1 cup bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup celery, thinly sliced on the bias
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook chow mein noodles until just shy of tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain, rinse briefly under cold water, and shake dry; toss with 1 tsp frying oil.
In a bowl, combine chicken, 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and sesame oil; mix to coat and marinate 10 minutes.
Make the sauce: whisk oyster sauce, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, white pepper, and chicken broth; set aside.
Heat a 12-inch wok or skillet over high until smoking. Add 1 tbsp frying oil. Stir-fry chicken in a single layer until browned and cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes; remove.
Add 1 tbsp frying oil, then garlic, ginger, and onion; stir-fry 30 seconds. Add cabbage, celery, and carrots; stir-fry until crisp-tender, 2 minutes.
Add noodles and bean sprouts; stir-fry, tossing to heat through, 1 to 2 minutes. Return chicken and add scallions.
Pour in sauce; stir-fry until noodles are evenly coated and glossy and sauce reduces, 1 to 2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, hot. If desired, drizzle a few drops of sesame oil to finish.

recipes.title: Chicken Congee
steps: MARINATING THE CHICKEN
In a bowl, add chicken, salt, white pepper, ginger juice and then mix it together well.
Set the chicken aside.
RINSE THE WHITE RICE
Rinse the rice in a metal bowl or pot a couple times and then drain the water.
BOILING THE WHITE RICE

Next add 8 cups of water and then set the stove on high heat until it is boiling. Once rice porridge starts to boil, set the stove on low heat and then stir it once every 8-10 minutes for around 20-25 minutes.
After 25 minutes, this is optional but you can add a little bit more water to make rice porridge to make it less thick or to your preference.
Next add the marinated chicken to the rice porridge and leave the stove on low heat for another 10 minutes.
After an additional 10 minutes add the green onions, sliced ginger, 1 pinch of salt, 1 pinch of white pepper and stir for 10 seconds.
Serve the rice porridge in a bowl
Optional: add Coriander on top of the rice porridge.

recipes.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
steps: Arrange cutlets between plastic and pound to 1/4-inch. Pat dry, then season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Lay 1 slice ham and 1 slice Swiss on each cutlet, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Tightly roll from the short end and secure with toothpicks; chill 10 minutes.
Prepare breading: place 1/2 cup flour in one dish. Beat 2 eggs with 1 tbsp water in a second. Mix breadcrumbs, Parmesan, and thyme in a third.
Dredge rolls in flour, dip in egg, then coat evenly in breadcrumb mixture. Rest 5 minutes to set the crust.
Heat frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat to 350°F. Sear rolls, turning, until golden on all sides, 4 to 5 minutes total.
Transfer to a rack on a sheet pan and bake at 375°F until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 15 to 18 minutes. Tent and rest 5 minutes; remove toothpicks.
Make sauce: melt 2 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 1 tbsp flour; cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in broth, then cream; simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Whisk in Dijon and lemon juice; season with pepper to taste. Spoon sauce over chicken and garnish with parsley before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Couscous
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for 1-2 mins just until softened. Add the chicken and fry for 7-10 mins until cooked through and the onions have turned golden.
