Grate over the ginger, stir through the harissa to coat everything and cook for 1 min more. Tip in the apricots, chickpeas and couscous, then pour over the stock and stir once.

Cover with a lid or tightly cover the pan with foil and leave for about 5 mins until the couscous has soaked up all the stock and is soft. Fluff up the couscous with a fork and scatter over the coriander to serve.
Serve with extra harissa, if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
steps: Cut each chicken breast in about 3 pieces, so that it cooks faster and put it in a small pot. Pour Enchilada sauce over it and cook covered on low to medium heat until chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes. No water is needed, the chicken will cook in the Enchilada sauce. Make sure you stir occasionally so that it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Remove chicken from the pot and shred with two forks.
Preheat oven to 375 F degrees.

Start layering the casserole. Start with about ¼ cup of the leftover Enchilada sauce over the bottom of a baking dish. I used a longer baking dish, so that I can put 2 corn tortillas across. Place 2 tortillas on the bottom, top with ⅓ of the chicken and ⅓ of the remaining sauce. Sprinkle with ⅓ of the cheese and repeat starting with 2 more tortillas, then chicken, sauce, cheese. Repeat with last layer with the remaining ingredients, tortillas, chicken, sauce and cheese.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes uncovered, until bubbly and cheese has melted and started to brown on top.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Chicken Enchiladas
ing: 2 oz serrano or jalapeño chiles, stemmed
1/2 cup cilantro leaves and stems, loosely packed
4 oz Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
1/4 cup white onion, finely diced, for garnish
steps: Simmer chicken in 4 cups broth with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper over medium heat until tender and 165°F in the thickest part, about 18–22 minutes. Transfer to a plate; reserve 1 cup cooking broth.
Shred chicken with two forks. Moisten with 2–3 tbsp reserved broth so it stays juicy; set aside.
Make salsa verde: Boil tomatillos, chiles, onion, and garlic in water to cover until tomatillos turn olive-green, 7–8 minutes. Drain well.
Blend boiled veg with cilantro, 1 tsp salt, cumin, and 1/2 cup reserved chicken broth until smooth. Adjust thickness with more broth if needed.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium. Pour in salsa and simmer, stirring, until it deepens and slightly thickens, 6–8 minutes. Season to taste; keep warm on low.

Warm 12 corn tortillas until pliable (skillet or 300°F oven, 5 minutes). Lightly oil a skillet with 1 tbsp oil over medium and quickly pass each tortilla in the hot oil 5–7 seconds per side to prevent tearing.
Dip a tortilla in warm salsa, place 2–3 tbsp shredded chicken down the center, sprinkle a little cheese, roll into a cylinder, and set seam-side down on a warm plate. Repeat with remaining tortillas.
Spoon more salsa over enchiladas, top with remaining cheese and let melt 1–2 minutes. Finish with crema, diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges; serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Fajita Mac and Cheese
steps: Fry your onion, peppers and garlic in olive oil until nicely translucent. Make a well in your veg and add your chicken. Add your seasoning and salt. Allow to colour slightly.
Add your cream, stock and macaroni.
Cook on low for 20 minutes. Add your cheeses, stir to combine.
Top with roasted peppers and parsley.

recipes.title: Chicken Fajitas
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced 1/2-inch thick
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
1 tbsp vegetable oil, as needed for frying
steps: In a bowl, combine lime juice, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, salt, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper. Add chicken and toss to coat; marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until just smoking, about 3 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil as needed, then spread chicken in an even layer.
Sear without stirring for 2 minutes, then cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, 5 to 6 minutes total. Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Add onion and bell peppers to the skillet with a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-high, stirring, until tender-crisp and lightly charred, 5 to 6 minutes.
Return chicken and any juices to the skillet. Toss with vegetables over medium heat until glossy and hot, about 1 minute. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side or wrap in foil and heat at 300°F for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and peppers sizzling-hot with warm tortillas, cilantro, and lime wedges. Let diners fill tortillas at the table.

recipes.title: Chicken Fricassée
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry and season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes.
Brown chicken skin-side down until deep golden, 5 to 7 minutes; flip and brown 3 minutes more. Work in batches, adding oil as needed. Transfer to a plate; pour off all but 1 tbsp fat.
Add mushrooms and cook over medium, stirring, until they release moisture and take color, 6 to 8 minutes. Add onion and cook until translucent, 4 minutes; stir in garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables; cook, stirring, 1 minute. Pour in wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes. Whisk in chicken stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken and accumulated juices, skin-side up. Cover and simmer gently over low heat until chicken reaches 175°F in the thickest thigh, 25 to 30 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate. Skim surface fat. Stir in cream and thyme; simmer uncovered over medium-low until slightly thickened and glossy, 5 to 7 minutes.
Off heat, stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Return chicken to sauce and warm 2 minutes over low heat.
Serve chicken napped with sauce; garnish with chopped parsley. Accompany with buttered noodles, rice, or potatoes.

recipes.title: Chicken Fried Rice
steps: Fried rice is best made with leftover rice that's at least a day old. Otherwise it becomes gummy in the skillet.

If you don’t have any leftover rice from the night before, cook a batch of rice and spread it on a large baking sheet or several large plates. Let the rice dry out for about 1 to 2 hours before using it for fried rice.

Rice sticks to the pan very easily, so make sure to use a wok or pan that doesn’t have a sticky surface. I usually cook stir-fries in my seasoned carbon steel wok, but cast iron or nonstick pans work well, too. You might need to add a little more oil if things aren’t releasing easily.
Prepare the chicken:

Chop the chicken into small 1/4-inch to 1/2-inch cubes. Sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon of salt over the chicken and mix to combine. Set the chicken aside for about 10 minutes (I usually use this time to chop all the vegetables).
Scramble the egg:

Heat a wok or large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Swirl in a tablespoon of oil and add the whisked eggs. Use a spatula to quickly scramble the eggs, breaking the curds into smaller pieces as they come together. Transfer the eggs to a plate.
Cook the chicken:
Add another tablespoon of oil in the wok or pan. Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat and transfer the cooked chicken to a plate.
Using your spatula, scrape off any chicken bits that are still stuck to the wok so they don't burn during the next step. You can also use paper towels to wipe down your wok or pan.
Cook the vegetables:

Swirl 1 tablespoon of oil into the wok over medium-high heat. Add the diced onions and cook them for 1 minute, until they start to soften. Mix in the minced garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the diced carrots and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and the peas, and stir to incorporate.
Cook the rice:

Add the rice to the wok or pan on top of the vegetables and stir to combine. Using the back of your spatula, smash any large chunks of rice to break them apart. Add the white and green parts of the sliced scallions (save the dark green parts) and five-spice powder. Stir to incorporate. If the rice starts to stick to the pan, stir in a little more oil.

Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the rice and stir to incorporate. Stir in the cooked chicken, scrambled eggs, and the dark parts of the scallions. Stir briefly to bring it together, and cook for another 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve:
Taste, and add more soy sauce if necessary. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Gyros
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, coriander, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and marinate 30 minutes (or up to 12 hours) refrigerated.
Make tzatziki: combine remaining 1/2 cup yogurt with squeezed cucumber, dill, red wine vinegar, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Chill until serving.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high and add frying oil as needed. Shake excess marinade and sear chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until browned and juices run clear.
Check doneness: cook chicken to an internal 165°F. Transfer to a board, rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Warm pitas in a dry skillet over medium or in a 350°F oven for 3 to 5 minutes until pliable.
Assemble gyros: spread tzatziki on warm pita, add sliced chicken, tomato, red onion, and lettuce.
Fold pita around fillings and serve immediately while warm.

recipes.title: Chicken Ham and Leek Pie
steps: Heat the chicken stock in a lidded saucepan. Add the chicken breast and bring to a low simmer. Cover with a lid and cook for 10 minutes. Remove the chicken breasts from the water with tongs and place on a plate. Pour the cooking liquor into a large jug.

Melt 25g/1oz of the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over a low heat. Stir in the leeks and fry gently for two minutes, stirring occasionally until just softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute. Add the remaining butter and stir in the flour as soon as the butter has melted. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.

Slowly pour the milk into the pan, just a little at a time, stirring well between each adding. Gradually add 250ml/10fl oz of the reserved stock and the wine, if using, stirring until the sauce is smooth and thickened slightly. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3 minutes.

Season the mixture, to taste, with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Remove from the heat and stir in the cream. Pour into a large bowl and cover the surface of the sauce with cling ilm to prevent a skin forming. Set aside to cool.
Preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6. Put a baking tray in the oven to heat.

For the pastry, put the flour and butter in a food processor and blend on the pulse setting until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. With the motor running, add the beaten egg and water and blend until the mixture forms a ball. Portion off 250g/10oz of pastry for the lid.

Roll the remaining pastry out on a lightly floured surface, turning the pastry frequently until around 5mm/¼in thick and 4cm/1½in larger than the pie dish. Lift the pastry over the rolling pin and place it gently into the pie dish. Press the pastry firmly up the sides, making sure there are no air bubbles. Leave the excess pastry overhanging the sides.

Cut the chicken breasts into 3cm/1¼in pieces. Stir the chicken, ham and leeks into the cooled sauce. Pour the chicken filling into the pie dish. Brush the rim of the dish with beaten egg. Roll out the reserved pastry for the lid.
Cover the pie with the pastry lid and press the edges together firmly to seal. Trim any excess pastry.

Make a small hole in the centre of the pie with the tip of a knife. Glaze the top of the pie with beaten egg. Bake on the preheated tray in the centre of the oven for 35-40 minutes or until the pie is golden-brown all over and the filling is piping hot.

recipes.title: Chicken Handi
steps: Take a large pot or wok, big enough to cook all the chicken, and heat the oil in it. Once the oil is hot, add sliced onion and fry them until deep golden brown. Then take them out on a plate and set aside.
To the same pot, add the chopped garlic and sauté for a minute. Then add the chopped tomatoes and cook until tomatoes turn soft. This would take about 5 minutes.
Then return the fried onion to the pot and stir. Add ginger paste and sauté well.
Now add the cumin seeds, half of the coriander seeds and chopped green chillies. Give them a quick stir.
Next goes in the spices – turmeric powder and red chilli powder. Sauté the spices well for couple of minutes.

Add the chicken pieces to the wok, season it with salt to taste and cook the chicken covered on medium-low heat until the chicken is almost cooked through. This would take about 15 minutes. Slowly sautéing the chicken will enhance the flavor, so do not expedite this step by putting it on high heat.

When the oil separates from the spices, add the beaten yogurt keeping the heat on lowest so that the yogurt doesn’t split. Sprinkle the remaining coriander seeds and add half of the dried fenugreek leaves. Mix well.
Finally add the cream and give a final mix to combine everything well.
Sprinkle the remaining kasuri methi and garam masala and serve the chicken handi hot with naan or rotis. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Chicken in Orange Sauce Recipe (Pollo a la Naranja)
steps: Place the olive oil and butter in a large sauce pan over medium heat. Add the chopped onions, red bell pepper and garlic. Cook for about 3 minutes, stirring often until the vegetables are soft.
Add the chicken legs and season with salt and pepper. Cook for about 1 minute on each side.

Add the chicken broth, orange juice and cook for about 2 minutes scraping the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Add the brown sugar and cover the pot. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for about 45 minutes or until chicken is cooked.
Spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve over white rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.title: Chicken Inasal
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin-on, scored
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Whisk cane vinegar, calamansi juice, lemon-lime soda, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, salt, pepper, soy sauce, and lemongrass. Reserve 1/4 cup for basting. Pour remaining over chicken and marinate 45 minutes at room temp.
Meanwhile, combine warm annatto oil with melted butter and 2 tbsp reserved marinade to make basting sauce; set aside. Lightly oil grill grates with frying oil.
Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to medium heat (375–400°F). Drain chicken well; pat dry to encourage browning.
Grill chicken skin side down over direct heat 6–8 minutes until lightly charred, moving to avoid flare-ups. Flip and grill 6 minutes more, basting with annatto-butter every 2–3 minutes.
Move chicken to indirect heat, cover, and cook 15–20 minutes, basting twice, until juices run clear and internal temp reaches 165°F at thickest part.
Finish skin side down over direct heat 1–2 minutes for crisping; baste once more and rest 5 minutes on a platter.
Warm any remaining basting sauce to a brief simmer for 1 minute and spoon over rested chicken.
Serve hot with lime wedges and steamed rice; spoon drippings over rice if desired.

recipes.title: Chicken Jalfrezi
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1 green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch strips
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch strips
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then add cumin seeds and bloom for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add onion and sauté over medium-high, stirring, until edges are deeply golden, 7 to 9 minutes. Stir in ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili; fry 30 seconds. Stir in tomato puree; cook down until glossy and thick, 3 to 4 minutes.
Increase heat to high; add chicken in a single layer. Sear without moving 2 minutes, then stir-fry until opaque on the outside, 3 minutes.
Add bell peppers and tomato wedges; stir-fry on high so liquids evaporate and vegetables stay crisp-tender, 4 to 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium; season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook, stirring once, until chicken reaches 165°F, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Uncover; sprinkle garam masala and lime juice. Toss over high heat to glaze and lightly char edges, 1 to 2 minutes. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Rest 2 minutes off heat, then garnish with cilantro and serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Jambalaya
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1-inch cubes
8 oz andouille sausage, halved lengthwise and sliced
1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
3/4 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
2 tbsp green onions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy 4- to 5-qt pot over medium-high until shimmering. Brown sausage 4 minutes; transfer to a plate. Add 1 tsp more oil if needed, then brown chicken 5 to 6 minutes until lightly colored.

Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until softened and golden at edges. Stir in garlic, paprika, thyme, salt, black pepper, and cayenne; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in rice to coat with aromatics; cook 1 minute. Return sausage and any juices. Add drained tomatoes and chicken broth; scrape up browned bits to deglaze.
Bring to a boil over medium-high, then cover, reduce to low, and simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
After 20 minutes, quickly uncover, gently fluff from bottom, re-cover, and continue to simmer on low for 5 to 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes to finish steaming. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Fluff again, fold in half the green onions, and serve hot, garnished with remaining green onions.

recipes.title: Chicken Karaage
steps: Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake and sugar to a bowl and whisk to combine. Add the chicken, then stir to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Add 1 inch of vegetable oil to a heavy bottomed pot and heat until the oil reaches 360 degrees F. Line a wire rack with 2 sheets of paper towels and get your tongs out. Put the potato starch in a bowl
Add a handful of chicken to the potato starch and toss to coat each piece evenly.

Fry the karaage in batches until the exterior is a medium brown and the chicken is cooked through. Transfer the fried chicken to the paper towel lined rack. If you want the karaage to stay crispy longer, you can fry the chicken a second time, until it's a darker color after it's cooled off once. Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Chicken Karahi
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into medium pieces
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for garnish
2 tbsp green chilies, thinly sliced, for garnish
1 tsp fresh ginger, julienned, for garnish
steps: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy karahi or wok over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add onion and sauté until just golden at the edges, 6–8 minutes.
Add chicken and sear, stirring, until opaque and lightly browned, 6–8 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Stir in chili powder, coriander, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook the spices in the oil for 30 seconds to bloom.
Add tomatoes and increase heat to high; cook, stirring, until tomatoes break down and release juices, 6–8 minutes.
Reduce to medium; cook uncovered, stirring often, until the gravy thickens and oil separates at the edges, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in yogurt over medium heat and cook until glossy and clinging to chicken, 3–4 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest pieces.
Fold in cilantro and half the green chilies and ginger. Simmer 2 minutes to meld flavors, then adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 2 minutes. Garnish with remaining green chilies, ginger, and cilantro. Serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Katsu
steps: Pat chicken dry, season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper, and let stand 5 minutes while you set up breading.
Set up three bowls: flour in one; beaten eggs in the second; panko in the third. Dredge chicken in flour, shake off excess.
Dip floured chicken in egg to coat, then press firmly into panko on both sides until evenly covered. Rest breaded cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a large skillet to 350°F over medium heat. Maintain 325–350°F during frying.
Fry 1–2 cutlets at a time until deeply golden, 3–4 minutes per side; turn once. Cook to an internal temperature of 165°F. Drain on a rack.
While cutlets rest 3 minutes, mound shredded cabbage on plates and portion hot rice alongside.
Slice katsu crosswise into 3/4-inch strips. Arrange over rice or beside cabbage.
Drizzle or serve with tonkatsu sauce and lemon wedges for squeezing at the table.

recipes.title: Chicken Kiev
ing: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 6-7 oz each
steps: Mash 8 tbsp butter with parsley, dill, lemon zest, and garlic until smooth. Shape into a 4x1-inch log, wrap, and freeze until very firm, about 20 minutes.
Trim chicken breasts. With a sharp knife, create a deep pocket from the thick side without piercing through. Season inside and out with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Cut the butter log into 4 equal batons. Insert one baton deep into each pocket. Press to seal, then tightly roll the breast around the butter, tucking sides in to enclose.
Set up breading: place 1/2 cup flour, 2 beaten eggs, and 1 cup breadcrumbs in separate shallow dishes. Dredge each roll in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere.
Repeat a second egg-and-breadcrumb pass for a thick seal. Chill the breaded rolls seam-side down until firm, 20 minutes, to help prevent leaking.
Heat 1/2 cup frying oil in a skillet over medium to 350°F. Shallow-fry rolls, turning, until golden on all sides, 4-6 minutes total. Transfer to a rack on a sheet pan.
Bake at 400°F until an instant-read thermometer in the thick center reads 165°F and butter just begins to sizzle, 12-15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes to set juices.
Serve immediately, slicing to reveal the herbed butter. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste if needed.

recipes.title: Chicken Korma
ing: 1.5 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked 20 minutes, drained
1/4 cup blanched almonds, soaked 20 minutes, drained
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tsp salt, and turmeric; cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes while you prep other ingredients.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium; add onions and cook, stirring, until deep golden, 15–18 minutes. Remove half for garnish; keep the rest in pot.
Add garlic and ginger; sauté 1 minute. Add coriander, cumin, cardamom, and chili powder; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Blend soaked cashews and almonds with 1/2 cup stock to a smooth paste. Add paste to pot; cook, stirring, 2–3 minutes until it thickens and ghee separates.
Add marinated chicken with all marinade; cook over medium-high, stirring, until opaque on the outside, 4–5 minutes.
Stir in remaining 1/2 cup stock, raisins, and sugar; bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook on low until chicken reaches 175°F at the thickest part, 20–25 minutes.
Uncover; stir in nutmeg, black pepper, remaining 1 tbsp ghee, and heavy cream. Simmer uncovered 3–5 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Adjust salt to taste.
Rest 5 minutes off heat. Garnish with reserved fried onions and cilantro; serve hot with steamed basmati rice or naan.

recipes.title: Chicken Laksa
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, sliced 1/2-inch
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 cup laksa leaves (Vietnamese coriander/daun kesum), chopped, for garnish
1 cup laksa paste, homemade or good-quality store-bought
steps: Soak 8 oz rice vermicelli in hot water until pliable, 6 to 8 minutes, then drain. Blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds just before serving to heat through.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil over medium heat. Add 1 cup laksa paste and fry, stirring, until aromatic and the oil splits, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 1 lb sliced chicken thighs and cook, stirring, until opaque on the outside, 3 minutes. Pour in 4 cups chicken stock and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in 1 cup coconut milk, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp fish sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes; do not boil hard to prevent splitting. Chicken should reach 165°F.
Add 4 oz tofu puffs and warm through, 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt or fish sauce as needed.
Blanch the soaked noodles for 30 seconds, then divide among 4 warmed bowls. Add a handful of bean sprouts to each bowl.
Ladle hot laksa broth and chicken over noodles, ensuring some tofu puffs in each bowl. Rest 1 minute to soften sprouts slightly.
Finish with 2 tbsp lime juice to the pot or to taste at the table. Serve with sambal oelek and scatter laksa leaves and cilantro generously over each bowl.

recipes.title: Chicken Liver Pate Recipe
steps: Clean livers of sinews and gall.
Put into a fireproof casserole with all other ingredients roughly chopped.
Season and cover with milk.
Put the lid on the casserole and cook in a slow oven (300ºF) for 2 hours.
Liquidize in a blender.
Adjust seasoning.
Add sherry or brandy.
Put in a dish and cover with melted butte

recipes.title: Chicken Lollipop
steps: Wash chicken with lemon
Drain and season chicken
Using shears, cut through the meat at the tip of the drumettes
Add all seasoning ingredients to the drumettes
Pour oil into a deep fryer, or saucepan to the level of about 5 inches so that the chicken will be submerged
Fry until medium brown, add your favorite sauce (I used honey garlic barbecue sauce) to place in the oven
Or fry until golden brown if you're not putting it in the oven
Using a silicon brush add sauce to chicken and place in the oven

recipes.title: Chicken Mandi
steps: Clean and cut the chicken; marinate briefly with salt, turmeric and a little oil.
Rinse and soak basmati rice 20–30 minutes.
In a large pot, heat ghee/oil. Fry chopped onion until golden. Add minced garlic and green chillies and fry 1–2 min.
Add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves) and ground spices (coriander, cumin). Stir until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces, brown lightly and add enough water/chicken stock to cover. Simmer until chicken is nearly cooked.
Remove chicken; measure remaining liquid and add soaked rice. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover and cook rice until almost done.
Return the chicken to the rice pot on top, cover tightly and steam on low for 10–15 min so flavors meld.

(Optional) For authentic smoky aroma: heat a small charcoal until red hot, place it on a small foil cup in the centre of the pot, add a tsp of butter/oil on the coal then cover immediately to trap smoke for 5–10 minutes. Remove coal.
Garnish with fried onions, chopped coriander and serve with chutney or raita.

recipes.title: Chicken Marengo
steps: Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish and stir-fry the mushrooms until they start to soften. Add the chicken legs and cook briefly on each side to colour them a little.
Pour in the passata, crumble in the stock cube and stir in the olives. Season with black pepper – you shouldn’t need salt. Cover and simmer for 40 mins until the chicken is tender.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pasta and a salad, or mash and green veg, if you like.

recipes.title: Chicken Marsala
ing: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded 1/2-inch thick
steps: Pat cutlets dry; season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Dredge lightly in 1/2 cup flour, shaking off excess.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Sear chicken in a single layer, 3 to 4 minutes per side, to 165°F. Transfer to a warm plate.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Sauté sliced mushrooms over medium-high, stirring, until browned and their liquid evaporates, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant, scraping browned bits from the pan with a wooden spoon.
Pour in 3/4 cup dry Marsala; boil, scraping up fond, until reduced by about half, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 3/4 cup chicken broth; simmer for 5 to 6 minutes until slightly syrupy and coats a spoon. Stir in 1 tsp lemon juice.
Return chicken and any juices to the pan; simmer, turning once, until warmed through and glazed, 2 minutes. Off heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter to silkiness.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and adjust seasoning to taste. Serve immediately with the pan sauce spooned over.

recipes.title: Chicken Milanese
ing: 1/4 cup olive oil, for frying, as needed
1 cup baby arugula, for garnish, as needed
steps: Lay chicken between plastic; pound to 1/4 inch. Pat dry and season both sides with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Set up dredging: shallow dish with flour; second with eggs beaten with milk and a pinch of salt; third with breadcrumbs mixed with Parmigiano, remaining salt, and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking excess; dip in egg; press into breadcrumb mixture until thoroughly coated. Rest coated cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/4 inch olive oil in a large skillet over medium to medium-high until shimmering, about 350°F.
Fry cutlets in batches without crowding, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through to 165°F internal. Adjust heat to maintain gentle sizzle.
Drain on a rack or paper towels; lightly season with a pinch of salt while hot.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; top each cutlet with a small handful of arugula and a drizzle of pan oil or fresh olive oil.

recipes.title: Chicken Mole Poblano
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 slice bolillo bread (or 1 oz French bread), torn
1 tbsp lard or frying oil, as needed
steps: Place chicken and 3 cups broth in a pot; add 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, cover, and cook until tender and 175°F at bone, about 35–40 minutes. Reserve meat and broth separately.

Toast ancho, pasilla, and mulato chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable and fragrant, 30–45 seconds per side. Soak in hot water for 15 minutes; drain, reserving 1/2 cup soaking liquid.

In the same skillet, add 1–2 tbsp lard or oil. Fry tortilla and bread until golden, 2–3 minutes; remove. Fry plantain slices until browned, 3–4 minutes; remove. Lightly fry onion and garlic until softened, 4–5 minutes; remove.
Toast sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, almonds, peanuts, and clove in the dry skillet over medium-low heat, 2–3 minutes, stirring; do not burn. Add raisins for last 30 seconds to plump.

Blend soaked chiles with tomato, fried onion and garlic, fried bread and tortilla, plantain, nuts and seeds, raisins, cinnamon, chocolate, 1 cup reserved broth, and 1/2 cup chile soaking liquid until very smooth, 1–2 minutes, adding broth as needed.
Heat 1 tbsp lard or oil in a wide pot over medium. Carefully pour in the puree; simmer and stir as it sputters until thickened, 10–12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in 1–1 1/2 cups reserved broth to reach a nappé sauce. Add chicken pieces, coat in mole, and simmer on low for 10–15 minutes to meld flavors, keeping at a gentle bubble.
Serve chicken ladled with mole and extra sauce. Sprinkle with a pinch of toasted sesame seeds if desired and accompany with warm tortillas and rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Panang Curry
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
6 kaffir lime leaves, 3 finely sliced, 3 torn
1 cup red bell pepper, thin strips
1/2 cup Thai basil leaves, loosely packed
steps: Chill 1/2 cup coconut milk until very cold, then open the can without shaking. Skim 1/2 cup thick cream from the top and set aside; reserve remaining coconut milk separately.
Warm 1 tsp peanut oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add the reserved thick coconut cream and cook, stirring, until it splits and the oil surfaces, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in 3 tbsp Panang curry paste and fry in the coconut oil, stirring constantly, until fragrant and glossy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add sliced chicken thighs and toss to coat in the paste. Cook until the exterior turns opaque, 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and 1 cup chicken broth. Add torn kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with 2 tsp palm sugar and 1 tbsp fish sauce. Add red bell pepper strips and simmer until chicken reaches 165°F and peppers are tender-crisp, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in sliced kaffir lime leaves and most of the Thai basil. Simmer 1 minute, then taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 2 minutes to settle. Garnish with remaining basil and serve hot over steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Paprikash
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
8 oz egg noodles, cooked for serving
steps: Pat chicken dry; season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high; brown chicken skin-side down 5 to 7 minutes, flip and brown 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and onions; cook, stirring, until soft and pale gold, 10 to 12 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds. Remove pot from heat; stir in sweet and hot paprika until onions are brick red.

Return pot to medium heat. Add broth and water; scrape up browned bits. Nestle chicken, skin-side up; bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 30 minutes, then uncover and simmer 10 minutes more, until chicken reaches 175°F.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate. Boil sauce over medium-high to reduce slightly, 5 minutes. In a bowl, whisk sour cream with flour until smooth and lump-free.

Off heat, whisk 1/2 cup hot sauce into sour cream mixture to temper. Return mixture to pot, whisking until velvety. Simmer gently over low 2 to 3 minutes; do not boil. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken to the pot, spoon with sauce, and warm 2 minutes over low. Meanwhile, cook egg noodles per package in salted water; drain well.
Serve chicken and generous paprika-cream sauce over noodles. Garnish with parsley and a final spoon of sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmentier
steps: For the topping, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain and push through a potato ricer, or mash thoroughly. Stir in the butter, cream and egg yolks. Season and set aside.

For the filling, melt the butter in a large pan. Add the shallots, carrots and celery and gently fry until soft, then add the garlic. Pour in the wine and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the tomato purée, chopped tomatoes and stock and cook for 10–15 minutes, until thickened. Add the shredded chicken, olives and parsley. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C Fan/Gas 4.
Put the filling in a 20x30cm/8x12in ovenproof dish and top with the mashed potato. Grate over the Gruyère. Bake for 30–35 minutes, until piping hot and the potato is golden-brown.

recipes.title: Chicken Parmesan
steps: Pound cutlets to 1/2-inch thickness if needed. Pat dry, then season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Set up dredge: bowl 1 flour; bowl 2 eggs beaten with 1 tbsp water; bowl 3 breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan, garlic powder, and oregano.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake excess; dip in egg; coat in breadcrumb-Parmesan mix, pressing to adhere. Rest breaded cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/4 inch vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 375°F. Fry cutlets in batches until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Drain on rack.
Warm marinara in a saucepan over medium heat until simmering, 3 to 5 minutes; keep hot.
Heat oven to 425°F. Spoon a thin layer of marinara in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Nestle cutlets, top each with sauce, then mozzarella slices. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Bake at 425°F until cheese is melted, bubbling, and chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest part, 10 to 12 minutes. Broil 1 to 2 minutes for added browning if desired.
Rest 5 minutes. Scatter basil over top and serve immediately with extra warm sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Chicken Piccata
ing: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pound chicken cutlets to 1/4-inch thickness between plastic. Pat dry. Season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Dredge cutlets lightly in flour, shaking off excess. Heat 2 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 2 minutes.
Sear cutlets in batches without crowding until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side, reaching 165°F internal. Transfer to a warm plate; tent loosely with foil. Add more oil if needed.
Pour off excess fat, leaving browned bits. Add wine; simmer over medium-high, scraping fond, until reduced by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, lemon juice, and zest; simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly syrupy.
Reduce heat to low. Add capers, then whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter, one piece at a time, to emulsify, 30 to 60 seconds. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cutlets and any juices to the pan; turn to coat and warm through for 1 minute over low heat.
Transfer to a platter. Spoon sauce over, garnish with parsley and lemon slices, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1-inch pieces
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Pat chicken dry, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high; brown chicken 4–5 minutes, stirring, until no pink on surface. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet; sauté onion, carrot, and celery with remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper until tender, 6–8 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables; cook, stirring, 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick and bubbly, 3–5 minutes.
Stir in browned chicken, peas, parsley, and thyme. Simmer 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste. Off heat, let filling cool 5 minutes.
Fit 1 pie dough round into a 9-inch pie dish; spoon in hot filling, mounding slightly. Top with second round; trim excess, fold under, and crimp. Cut 4–5 slits for steam.
Place pie on a rimmed sheet. Bake at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling. Ensure chicken pieces reach 165°F.
Let rest 10 minutes to set. Slice and serve warm.

recipes.title: Chicken Pozole
ing: 1 cup packed cilantro, tender stems and leaves
2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 (25 oz) cans white hominy, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup radishes, thinly sliced, for garnish
1/2 cup white onion, finely diced, for garnish
steps: Season 1.5 lb chicken thighs with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium-high and brown chicken 4–5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add 8 cups chicken stock and return chicken to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 25 minutes, skimming foam. Cook to 175°F at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, broil tomatillos, jalapeños, and poblano on a sheet 4–6 inches from heat, turning until blistered, 6–8 minutes. Cool, then peel poblano if desired.
Blend broiled tomatillos, jalapeños, poblano, 1 cup onion, 4 cloves garlic, 1 cup cilantro, 1 tbsp oregano, and 2 tsp cumin until very smooth, 45–60 seconds.

Remove chicken to a plate. Strain and reserve broth if needed. Shred meat, discarding skin and bones. Return pot to medium heat, add a little oil, and fry the green sauce, stirring, until thickened and darker, 5–7 minutes.
Pour reserved broth into the fried sauce and bring to a simmer. Stir in hominy and shredded chicken. Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes; adjust salt and pepper to taste. Add lime juice to brighten.
Warm bowls. Ladle pozole and let stand 2 minutes to settle flavors. Serve hot with shredded cabbage, radishes, diced onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges for squeezing.

recipes.title: Chicken Quesadillas
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, finely chopped
steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano; toss well. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then add chicken and cook, stirring, until browned and cooked to 165°F, 6 to 8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook until translucent, 3 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds. Fold in tomatoes and cilantro; cook until most moisture evaporates, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Wipe skillet and heat over medium. Warm tortillas 30 seconds per side to make pliable. Keep covered with a towel.
Assemble each quesadilla: spread 2 tbsp mixed cheeses on half of a tortilla, add 1/4 cup chicken mixture, top with 2 more tbsp cheese, and fold to close.
Add a thin film of oil to skillet over medium. Cook folded quesadillas in batches until tortillas are spotty golden and cheese melts, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Adjust heat to prevent scorching.
Hold finished quesadillas on a rack or sheet at 200°F while cooking remaining batches to keep crisp.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve hot with lime wedges. Salt to taste if needed.

recipes.title: Chicken Quinoa Greek Salad
steps: Cook the quinoa following the pack instructions, then rinse in cold water and drain thoroughly.

Meanwhile, mix the butter, chilli and garlic into a paste. Toss the chicken fillets in 2 tsp of the olive oil with some seasoning. Lay in a hot griddle pan and cook for 3-4 mins each side or until cooked through. Transfer to a plate, dot with the spicy butter and set aside to melt.

Next, tip the tomatoes, olives, onion, feta and mint into a bowl. Toss in the cooked quinoa. Stir through the remaining olive oil, lemon juice and zest, and season well. Serve with the chicken fillets on top, drizzled with any buttery chicken juices.

recipes.title: Chicken Rendang
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin-on, cut into large chunks
3 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
8 oz fresh grated coconut (kerisik), toasted until deep golden
3 stalks lemongrass, white parts only, bruised
1 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, to taste
steps: Make the spice paste: blend soaked dried chilies, fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, and turmeric with 2 tbsp oil and a splash of water until very smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium. Fry the spice paste and bruised lemongrass, stirring, until thick, aromatic, and the oil splits, about 10–12 minutes.
Add chicken and turn to coat, cooking until no longer pink on the outside, about 4–5 minutes. Stir in coconut milk and water; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add kaffir lime leaves, salt, and palm sugar. Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring every 5–7 minutes, until sauce is reduced and glossy, about 45 minutes.
Stir in toasted grated coconut (kerisik). Continue to cook on low, stirring frequently, until the gravy turns dark, thick, and clings to the chicken, 20–30 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with salt and white pepper to taste. Continue cooking until chicken is very tender and sauce is almost dry, 5–10 minutes more.
For food safety, ensure chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes off heat before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Saag
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp cilantro, chopped, for garnish, as needed
steps: Blanch greens: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add spinach and cook for 1 minute. Drain, shock in ice water, squeeze dry, then blend with 1/2 cup water to a coarse puree.
Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine yogurt, 1/2 tsp salt, half the ginger, and half the garlic. Add chicken, coat well, and rest for 15 minutes while you start the sauce.
Build masala: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in onion and cook until golden, 8–10 minutes.

Add aromatics and spices: Add remaining ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute. Stir in coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili; cook 30 seconds. Add tomato and cook until thick and glossy, 4–5 minutes.
Brown chicken: Add marinated chicken with any yogurt. Cook over medium-high, stirring, until no longer pink on the outside, 4–5 minutes.
Simmer with spinach: Stir in spinach puree and 1/2 tsp salt. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender, stirring once or twice.
Finish and adjust: Uncover, simmer to desired thickness, 3–5 minutes. Stir in garam masala, black pepper, and lemon juice. Rest 2 minutes off heat.
Serve: Garnish with chopped cilantro and a drizzle of ghee if desired. Serve hot with basmati rice or roti.

recipes.title: Chicken Salad Sandwich
ing: 1 lb cooked chicken breast, finely chopped
1/4 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/8 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Combine 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tbsp sour cream, 2 tsp Dijon, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Fold in 1 lb finely chopped cooked chicken, 1 stalk diced celery, 2 tbsp minced red onion, and 1 tbsp chopped parsley until evenly coated.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste; if desired, thin with 1–2 tsp water to reach a creamy but scoopable consistency.
Lay out 8 toasted bread slices; place a lettuce leaf on 4 slices to keep bread crisp.
Mound about 1/2 cup chicken salad on each lettuce-lined slice and spread to edges.
Top with remaining bread slices, press gently, and cut sandwiches in halves or thirds.
Serve immediately, or chill assembled sandwiches for 10 minutes to set before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Salad With Mushrooms and Bacon
steps: Place chicken breast in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, add 1 tsp salt and simmer for approximately 15 minutes. Allow chicken to cool and then shred meat with two forks.
Finely chop shallot/red onion.
Stir mayonnaise, crème fraîche, Dijon mustard and apple cider vinegar to combine. Season with salt, pepper and extra Dijon mustard to taste. Combine with onion and chicken.
Fry bacon until crisp and transfer to plate lined with paper towels.
Rinse mushrooms, slice and fry in the same pan as bacon until golden (approximately 5 minutes). Season with a bit of salt and pepper.
Arrange your chicken salad in a serving dish, topped with crisp bacon, mushrooms and chopped parsley. Serve on a slice of light or dark bread.

recipes.title: Chicken Saltimbocca
ing: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season both sides with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, then lightly dredge in 1/2 cup flour, shaking off excess.
Lay 2 sage leaves on each cutlet and top with 2 slices prosciutto, pressing so prosciutto adheres; if needed, secure with toothpicks.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until foaming, 1 minute. Add cutlets prosciutto-side down; cook 2 to 3 minutes until lightly crisp.
Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until chicken is just cooked through to 165°F. Transfer to a warm plate; tent loosely with foil.
Pour off excess fat, then add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Deglaze with 1/2 cup white wine over medium heat, scraping browned bits, and reduce by half, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup broth and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly syrupy. Stir in remaining 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp lemon juice off heat; swirl until glossy.
Return cutlets to the pan, spoon sauce over, and warm 30 to 60 seconds. Discard toothpicks. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Transfer to plates, spoon pan sauce over, and garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Satay
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, trimmed and 1-inch cubed
10 oz roasted unsalted peanuts, finely ground
1 tbsp roasted peanuts, chopped, for garnish
steps: Soak 12 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes. In a bowl, whisk 1/3 cup kecap manis, 2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 3 tbsp coconut milk, garlic, ginger, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken to the marinade, toss to coat, and chill for 20 minutes while you make the sauce. Thread marinated chicken tightly onto soaked skewers.

Make peanut sauce: In a saucepan, combine ground peanuts, 1 1/2 cups hot water, 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tbsp kecap manis, and 1 tbsp palm sugar. Simmer over medium-low, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Adjust sauce with a splash of water for dipping consistency; keep warm over low. Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 425°F). Brush grates lightly with frying oil.
Grill skewers 3–4 minutes per side, basting lightly with a little kecap manis in the last minute. Cook until chicken reaches 165°F at the center, 8–10 minutes total.
Rest skewers 3 minutes. If desired, briefly warm a few spoonfuls of sauce on the grill to pick up smoke, stirring back into the pot.
Serve skewers with warm peanut sauce, chopped roasted peanuts, cilantro, and lime wedges. Spoon a little sauce over and squeeze lime just before eating.

recipes.title: Chicken Schnitzel
steps: Pound chicken cutlets between plastic wrap to 1/4-inch thickness using a mallet; pat dry.
Set up breading: place flour in one shallow dish; beat eggs with milk, salt, and pepper in a second; place breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess; dip in egg, letting excess drip; press into breadcrumbs to coat evenly. Rest 5 minutes.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet over medium to medium-high heat to 350°F.
Fry 1–2 cutlets at a time without crowding until deeply golden and cooked through, about 2–3 minutes per side; internal temp 165°F.
Transfer to a rack or paper towels; season lightly with a pinch of salt while hot. Repeat, keeping oil at 325–350°F.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; sprinkle with parsley just before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma with homemade garlic herb yoghurt sauce
steps: Start by cutting your chicken up into reasonably small slices. Grab your ziplock bag and dump the freshly sliced chicken inside.

Add garlic, coriander, cumin, cardomom, cayenne pepper, paprika, salt, pepper, lemon juice and olive oil to the bag. Close the bag and mix thoroughly. Place in fridge for 10-12 hours (shorter is fine but longer is better).

Once ready to cook, heat your fry pan to medium-high and add a tiny bit of olive oil. Fry one side of all of your flatbreads until slightly toasty. Remove from pan, add enough oil to coat the fry pan. Put crumble fries into air fryer on 180 for 15 minutes shaking occasionally.

The pan should be pretty hot by now, add the chicken in 2 batches (unless you have a big fry pan) to avoid overcrowding. The chicken should get a nice sear and darker colour which is perfect. Cook for a further 5-8 minutes or until cooked through. Repeat with next chicken batch.

While chicken is cooking, place your Greek yoghurt into a bowl. Combine garlic, finely chopped mint and parsley, squeeze or so of lemon and cumin. Combine and add salt to taste. In a small bowl, combine 1tsp garlic powder, paprika, cumin, onion powder, oregano, dried parsley, cayenne pepper (optional) mix and leave aside for fries.

Season fries immediately once cooked and add salt to taste. Once the chicken is complete, serve immediately by laying out your flatbread, spreading the sauce evenly over the bread, add lettuce, onion, tomato, fries, chicken, feta and more sauce on top. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken Souvlaki
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, trimmed and 1 1/2-inch cubed
1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt, for serving
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for serving
8 oz cherry tomatoes, for optional skewering or side
steps: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes. In a bowl, whisk 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, fresh and dried oregano, garlic, lemon zest, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken cubes to the marinade, toss to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes (or up to 2 hours for deeper flavor).
Thread chicken onto soaked skewers, packing pieces snugly but not overly tight; optionally alternate with cherry tomatoes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 400°F). Oil grates lightly. Grill skewers 8 to 10 minutes total, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and juices run clear.
Check doneness: chicken must reach 165°F at the thickest piece. If needed, continue grilling 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Rest skewers 3 minutes. In a small bowl, mix 1/2 cup yogurt with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a quick sauce.
Serve souvlaki hot with lemon wedges for squeezing, yogurt sauce, and warmed pita or a simple salad if desired.

recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Olives and Preserved Lemon
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin on, trimmed
1 preserved lemon, rind only, rinsed and sliced
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for garnish as needed
steps: In a bowl, combine garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, coriander, saffron, pepper, salt, 2 tbsp olive oil, and lemon juice to form a paste. Rub paste over chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a tagine or heavy Dutch oven over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add onions and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, about 8 minutes.
Nestle chicken skin side down over onions and sear until skin is lightly browned, about 4 minutes. Flip chicken, add broth, and scatter cilantro and parsley over.
Cover with lid and reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 35 minutes, maintaining a gentle bubble; do not boil vigorously.
Stir in olives and preserved lemon rind. Re-cover and simmer until chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest part and is very tender, 10 to 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 3 to 5 minutes to slightly reduce sauce until glossy and spoonable. Skim excess fat if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt or a squeeze of lemon if needed. Rest off heat 3 minutes.
Serve hot, sprinkled with chopped cilantro as needed, with couscous or crusty bread.

recipes.title: Chicken Teriyaki
ing: 1 tsp sesame seeds, for garnish, optional
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish, optional
steps: Stir soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a bowl until sugar dissolves; reserve 2 tbsp separately for finishing glaze.
Pat chicken dry and lightly season with black pepper. Warm a large skillet over medium heat and add a thin film of frying oil.
Place chicken skin side down and cook without moving until skin is deep golden and crisp, about 7–8 minutes. Spoon off excess fat as needed.
Flip chicken and cook until juices run clear and internal temperature reaches 165°F, about 5–6 minutes more.
Pour the larger portion of sauce into the skillet. Simmer, turning chicken, until bubbling vigorously and reduced, about 2–3 minutes.
Whisk water and cornstarch, then stir into skillet. Add reserved 2 tbsp sauce and simmer until glossy and syrupy, 1–2 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a board, rest 2 minutes, then slice into bite-size strips. Return slices to skillet and toss to coat, 30 seconds.
Plate chicken over rice if desired, spooning sauce over. Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka
ing: 1.75 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and 1.5-inch chunks
steps: Whisk yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, oil, Kashmiri chili, coriander, cumin, garam masala, paprika, salt, turmeric, and pepper until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add chicken and red onion, toss to coat, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour (up to 12 hours) for best flavor.
Thread chicken and onion onto soaked skewers, packing pieces snugly but not tight. Rest at room temperature for 15 minutes while heating grill.
Preheat a gas grill to medium-high (about 425°F) or prepare a hot charcoal fire with a two-zone setup; oil grates just before grilling.
Grill skewers over direct heat, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly charred, 8 to 10 minutes total.
Move to indirect heat, baste lightly with melted ghee, and cook covered until chicken reaches 165°F internal temperature, 4 to 6 minutes more.
Transfer to a platter, rest 5 minutes, then squeeze lemon over and sprinkle with cilantro to taste.
Serve hot with onion, lemon wedges, and optional green chutney or naan.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ing: 1.5 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
steps: Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin, paprika, coriander, 1 tsp salt, and pepper. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and chill for 30 to 60 minutes.
Prepare aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp oil and butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Bloom spices: Add turmeric, remaining 1 tbsp garam masala, remaining 1 tsp cumin, and Kashmiri chili. Cook, stirring, 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
Build sauce: Stir in crushed tomatoes, water, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Sear chicken: Heat a broiler to high (or grill to medium-high). Thread chicken on a rack-lined tray brushed with oil. Broil 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred and 160°F.
Finish masala: Slide seared chicken and any juices into the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender.
Enrich and season: Stir in heavy cream; simmer 2 minutes. Season with salt to taste. If too thick, loosen with a splash of water.
Serve: Rest 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with basmati rice or naan.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinga Tacos
ing: 3 oz canned chipotle chiles in adobo, with sauce
4 oz queso fresco, crumbled, for garnish
1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Place chicken in a pot with 1/2 cup broth and a pinch of salt; bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 12–15 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then shred.
While chicken cooks, char tomatoes, onion slices, and garlic in a dry skillet over medium-high, turning until blistered (6–8 minutes). Peel any very blackened tomato skins if desired.
Blend charred tomatoes, onion, garlic, chipotles with adobo, remaining 1/2 cup broth, oregano, cumin, 1 tsp salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium. Pour in the sauce; simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until slightly thick and glossy.
Stir in shredded chicken; simmer 3–4 minutes to coat and heat through. Adjust salt and chipotle to taste; the tinga should be saucy, not dry.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry skillet over medium for 30–45 seconds per side until pliable.
Assemble tacos: spoon tinga into tortillas and top with queso fresco and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
Optional: keep tinga warm over low heat, adding a splash of broth if it thickens. Keep tortillas wrapped in a towel.

recipes.title: Chicken Tinola
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken pieces, cut into serving pieces
2 oz fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cups green papaya, peeled and cut into 1-inch wedges
2 cups water spinach leaves (or spinach), roughly torn
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, to taste
2 long green chilies (siling pansigang), slit lengthwise
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium; brown chicken pieces 3 to 4 minutes per side to render fat and add flavor.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent and ginger fragrant, about 3 minutes, scraping browned bits.
Pour in 6 cups chicken broth and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through to 165°F.
Stir in fish sauce and pepper. Taste and adjust salt to balance salinity and ginger heat.
Add green papaya wedges and slit green chilies; simmer uncovered until papaya is just tender but not mushy, 10 to 12 minutes.
Skim excess fat. Turn off heat and stir in water spinach leaves until just wilted, about 30 seconds.
Ladle hot tinola into bowls, ensuring a mix of broth, chicken, papaya, and greens. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
ing: 4 oz corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium and pan-fry tortilla strips in batches until crisp and lightly golden, 3–4 minutes; drain on paper towels and set aside.
In the same pot, char tomatoes, onion, and garlic over medium-high, turning until lightly blistered, 6–8 minutes. Blend with chipotle and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Return puree to the pot with remaining 3 cups broth. Nestle in chicken thighs, bring to a boil, then lower to a steady simmer for 25–30 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F.
Transfer chicken to a plate; cool slightly, then remove skin and bones and shred meat. Skim excess fat from soup if desired.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice; simmer 5 minutes to marry flavors.
To serve, divide crispy tortilla strips among bowls. Ladle hot soup over to soften some strips while keeping others crisp.
Garnish each bowl with queso fresco, crema, avocado, and cilantro. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges if desired.

recipes.title: Chicken Vindaloo
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed, cut into 2-inch pieces
8 dried Kashmiri red chilies, stems removed
steps: Make the spice paste: Toast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, mustard seeds, and cloves in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant; cool, then grind to a powder.

Soak Kashmiri chilies in 1/2 cup hot water for 10 minutes. Blend chilies with soaking liquid, ground spices, garlic, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, vinegar, tamarind paste, jaggery, salt, and pepper to a smooth paste.
Marinate chicken: Toss chicken with 2/3 of the paste in a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 8 hours) to season deeply.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onions and cook, stirring, until deeply golden, 10 to 12 minutes; add remaining oil if needed.
Add remaining vindaloo paste to onions and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates and the paste darkens slightly, stirring constantly to avoid scorching.
Add marinated chicken and any juices; sear 4 to 5 minutes, turning to coat well. Add 1 cup water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes.
Uncover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes more to thicken. Stir occasionally until sauce is glossy and chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes. Adjust salt, jaggery, or vinegar to balance heat, tang, and sweetness. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice or warm flatbread.

recipes.title: Chicken wings with cumin, lemon & garlic
steps: Using a pair of sharp kitchen scissors, cut each wing at the knuckle into two pieces. Mix the garlic, lemon zest and juice, cumin and oil with plenty of seasoning, then tip into a dish with the chicken wings and toss to coat.
Cover and put in the fridge to marinate for at least 1 hr, or overnight if you have time. Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6, or heat an outdoor barbecue.
Bake the chicken wings on an oven tray for 45-50 mins until crisp, or barbecue for 20 mins, drizzling over the honey for the final 10 mins of each method.
Serve on a platter with plenty of paper napkins. Fill small bowls with olives, pistachios or almonds, dates and pickled chillies and flatbreads to serve alongside, along with the dishes below.

recipes.title: Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts
steps: Heat a large frying pan on a high heat and season the chicken. Add the olive oil to the pan, then the chicken. Brown for about 5 mins on each side, remove onto a plate, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. In the remaining fat, fry the onions for 3 mins, then add the garlic and saffron. Cook for 3-4 mins more. Add the sherry, then simmer for 3-5 mins until syrupy.

Put the chicken leg pieces back into the pan, tip in the stock, thyme and raisins, cover, then gently cook on a low heat for 20 mins. Add the breast meat and any juices left on the plate. Simmer for 10 mins more until cooked through and the sauce in the pan has reduced.

While the chicken is cooking, heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Scatter the pine nuts over a baking sheet, then roast for 10 mins until golden and toasted. Once the chicken has cooked through, season to taste, scatter with pine nuts and parsley, then serve with rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Xacuti
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into 10 pieces
6 dried Kashmiri red chilies, stems removed
steps: Marinate chicken with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric from the measured turmeric; set aside for 20 minutes while you prep.
Dry-roast chilies, coriander, cumin, peppercorns, poppy and fennel seeds in a skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant; remove to cool.
In same skillet, toast grated coconut over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until golden; add nutmeg in last 30 seconds. Cool.
Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium; sauté onions for 10 minutes until deep golden. Reserve half for garnish; leave half in pan.
Blend roasted spices, toasted coconut, sautéed onions (half left in pan), garlic, ginger, remaining turmeric, tamarind, and 3/4 cup water to a smooth paste.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan, pour in the spice paste, and fry over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until it releases oil and darkens.
Add chicken and 1/4 cup water; stir to coat. Cover and simmer over medium-low for 25 to 30 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender.
Stir in coconut milk and reserved onions; simmer for 5 minutes to meld. Adjust salt to taste and thin with a splash of water if needed. Rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with Goan pao or steamed rice.

recipes.title: Chicken Yassa
ing: 2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup mustard, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss with 2 lb chicken and 2 sliced onions. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours refrigerated.
Remove chicken and onions from marinade, reserving all liquids and onions. Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt. Blot onions if very wet to encourage browning.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add the marinated onions to the pot. Cook, stirring, until softened and caramelized at edges, 10 to 12 minutes. Do not burn; reduce heat if needed.
Return chicken to pot. Stir in reserved marinade, 1 cup chicken broth, 1 bay leaf, and lemon rounds. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part.
Uncover and simmer 5 to 8 minutes to thicken to a glossy sauce that coats a spoon. Adjust salt, pepper, and lemon to taste.
Discard bay leaf. Serve hot over steamed rice, garnish with chopped parsley.

recipes.title: Chicken à la King
ing: 1 lb chicken breast, cut in 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup jarred pimentos, drained and sliced
4 cups cooked egg noodles, hot, for serving
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Pat chicken dry, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and sear until no longer pink and reaches 165°F, 4–6 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp oil and mushrooms to the skillet; cook over medium-high, stirring, until browned and their liquid evaporates, 5–6 minutes. Transfer to the plate with chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt butter in the skillet. Sprinkle in flour and cook, stirring constantly, until pale golden and nutty, 2–3 minutes.
Whisk in sherry; simmer 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then milk; bring to a gentle boil, whisking, and simmer until slightly thickened, 4–5 minutes.
Stir in cream, remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper; simmer 2 minutes. Return chicken and mushrooms with any juices; simmer until heated through and sauce coats a spoon, 2–3 minutes.
Fold in peas, pimentos, and parsley; warm 1–2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve spooned generously over hot egg noodles.

recipes.title: Chickpea Fajitas
steps: Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6 and line a baking tray with foil. Drain the chickpeas, pat dry and tip onto the prepared baking tray. Add the oil and paprika, toss to coat, then roast for 20-25 mins until browned and crisp, shaking halfway through cooking.

Meanwhile, put the tomatoes and onion in a small bowl with the vinegar and set aside to pickle. Put the avocado in another bowl and mash with a fork, leaving some larger chunks. Stir in the lime juice and season well. Mix the soured cream with the harissa and set aside until ready to serve.
Heat a griddle pan until nearly smoking. Add the tortillas , one at a time, charring each side until hot with griddle lines.

Put everything on the table and build the fajitas : spread a little of the harissa cream over the tortilla, top with roasted chickpeas, guacamole, pickled salsa and coriander, if you like. Serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

recipes.title: Chickpea, chorizo & spinach stew
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan, then gently fry the onion for 3-4 mins until it begins to soften. Stir in the carrot, celery, thyme and bay leaves. Season, then cook for 2-3 mins, stirring occasionally.

Add the garlic, chorizo, cinnamon and smoked paprika. Gently fry until the vegetables soften and the chorizo starts to release its oils and crisp up. Stir in the chickpeas, vinegar and 150ml water, then bring to a simmer for 1-2 mins until the chickpeas have heated up.
Add the spinach, then stir through the chickpeas until it wilts a little. Remove from the heat, season to taste, then serve warm with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Chilean Dobladitas
steps: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet.
Whisk flour, 1 cup melted butter, milk, baking powder, and salt together in a bowl until begins to pull together. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface; knead until smooth and elastic.

Roll dough out to ⅛-inch thickness; cut into 8-inch circles. Brush circles with remaining 3 tablespoons melted butter. Fold each circle in half, then fold in half again to form triangles. Press firmly to seal the layers; place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 15 minutes. Serve warm

recipes.title: Chilean Empanada
steps: Make the filling: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook and stir until onion is golden brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Add pork and cook until completely browned and crumbly, 7 to 10 minutes more. Drain fat from the skillet. Stir in raisins, olives, and hard-cooked eggs.
Whisk water and cornstarch together in a small bowl; pour into the skillet and stir until liquid thickens. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Make the dough: Whisk milk and melted shortening together in a bowl until evenly blended. Stir flour and salt together in a separate large bowl. Pour milk mixture into flour mixture; whisk until well combined and a dough forms. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/8 inch. Cut into 12 circles with a round cookie cutter or glass. Spoon filling into the center of each circle. Fold each circle in half and press the edges with a fork to seal. Brush the tops with beaten egg. Place empanadas onto the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Chilean-Style Sopaipillas
steps: Peel, seed, and cut zapallo into chunks. Place in a saucepan, cover with water, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cook until zapallo is soft and easily pierced with a fork, 15 to 20 minutes. Drain and allow to cool slightly.

Mix flour, baking soda, and salt together in a mixing bowl, and set aside. Stir together squash and melted butter. Stir the flour mixture into the butter mixture until blended. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until soft and satiny, adding a little more flour if necessary. Cover dough with a towel and allow to rest 15 minutes.
Roll out the dough to 1/8-inch thick, and cut into 3-inch diameter circles. Poke each circle a few times with a fork to make holes and prevent rising.

Pour oil into a large, deep skillet and heat over medium-high heat until hot, 385 degrees F (195 degrees C). Place several of the dough circles into hot oil; cook until lightly browned, 3 to 4 minutes. Drain on paper towels. Cook remainder of dough circles in batches.

recipes.title: Chiles Rellenos
ing: 10 oz Oaxaca cheese, cut into 8 batons
1 lb ripe Roma tomatoes, cored and quartered
1/2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
steps: Char poblanos over an open flame or under a broiler set to High, turning until blistered and blackened on all sides, 6–8 minutes. Transfer to a covered bowl to steam for 10 minutes.
Gently peel charred skins. Slit each chile lengthwise and remove seeds and membranes, keeping stems intact. Pat dry.
Tuck a baton of Oaxaca cheese into each chile. Lightly dust chiles with 2 tbsp of the flour to help batter adhere; set aside.
Blend tomatoes, onion, garlic, vegetable broth, sugar, and 1/2 tsp salt until smooth. Simmer in a saucepan over medium heat for 12–15 minutes; stir in vinegar and keep warm on low.
Whip egg whites with a clean bowl and whisk to stiff peaks, 3–4 minutes. Beat yolks with remaining flour, 1/2 tsp salt, and pepper, then gently fold into whites to make a fluffy batter.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet to 350°F. Dip each stuffed chile in batter, letting excess drip, and fry seam side down until golden, 2–3 minutes per side. Drain on a rack.
Nestle fried chiles into the warm tomato sauce and simmer gently for 2 minutes to meld. Cheese should be melted; internal temp should reach 165°F for safety.
Serve chiles napados (sauced) on plates; garnish with cilantro. Eat immediately while exterior is crisp and interior is molten.

recipes.title: Chili con Carne
ing: 2 lb beef chuck, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
3 tbsp chili powder (New Mexican or ancho)
steps: Pat beef dry, season with 1 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high until shimmering, then brown beef in batches, 6–8 minutes total, adding oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and a pinch of salt; cook, stirring, until translucent, 5–6 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add chili powder, cumin, oregano, and cayenne; toast, stirring, 45–60 seconds. Stir in tomato paste; cook 1 minute to darken slightly.

Return beef and any juices to pot. Pour in broth and water, scraping up browned bits. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer; cover partially and simmer for 60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Uncover and continue to simmer until beef is very tender and sauce thickens, 20–30 minutes more. Skim fat if desired.
Stir in vinegar and brown sugar. Mix 1 tbsp masa harina with 2 tbsp water; stir into chili and simmer 5 minutes to lightly thicken. Adjust salt to 1 tbsp total to taste.
Ensure beef is tender and hot; serve hot with optional garnishes (chopped onion, jalapeño, cilantro), and warm tortillas on the side.

recipes.title: Chilli ginger lamb chops
steps: Put the garlic in a bowl with the ginger, lemon juice, oil, spices and seasoning. Blitz with a hand blender until smooth, then use to coat the lamb chops on both sides.

Leave to marinate in the fridge for a couple of hours or overnight. Heat a barbecue until hot. Barbecue the chops over the coals for 3 mins on each side until cooked but still pink and juicy in the centre.

recipes.title: Chilli prawn linguine
steps: Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cook the pasta according to the packet instructions. Add the sugar snap peas for the last minute or so of cooking time.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan, toss in the garlic and chilli and cook over a fairly gentle heat for about 30 seconds without letting the garlic brown. Tip in the prawns and cook over a high heat, stirring frequently, for about 3 minutes until they turn pink.

Add the tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 minutes until they just start to soften. Drain the pasta and sugar snaps well, then toss into the prawn mixture. Tear in the basil leaves, stir, and season with salt and pepper.
Serve with salad leaves drizzled with the lime dressing, and warm crusty bread.

recipes.title: Chinese Orange Chicken
steps: Make the orange sauce:
Whisk together sauce ingredients in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Prep the chicken:
Cut chicken into about 1-inch cubes. Whisk eggs with salt and black pepper in a bowl and add chicken. Stir together.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour and cornstarch. Remove chicken from eggs with a slotted spoon or tongs, letting excess egg drain off, then transfer to cornstarch mixture and coat well.
Fry the chicken:

Add oil to a large 10- to 12-inch skillet. Heat over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F. If you don’t have a thermometer, you can also test the temperature by sprinkling in some flour. If the oil is hot enough, it should fizzle immediately.

Once oil is hot, fry the chicken in two batches. The oil might not completely cover the chicken—that’s okay. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip the chicken pieces and cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 3 to 4 more minutes. Total cook time is about 6 to 8 minutes.
Remove fried chicken cubes and transfer to a plate lined with paper towels, so the chicken can drain. Repeat until all the chicken is cooked.
Simmer the chicken in the sauce:

Once chicken is done, pour out hot oil and wipe pan clean. Add a fresh tablespoon of oil along with chopped garlic and shallot. Cook for a minute and then add the sauce. Simmer the sauce until it starts to thicken.

Once the sauce is lightly bubbling, add fried chicken and toss together to coat. The sauce should continue to thicken and stick to the chicken. Let simmer for a minute or two more. Serve orange chicken over cooked white rice, garnished with sesame seeds and fresh scallions.
Did you love this recipe? Let us know with a rating and review!

LEFTOVERS! The orange chicken keeps well in the fridge for 5 days. Reheat in a skillet with a splash of water over low heat. Freeze the orange chicken for up to 3 months, but be sure to thaw it before reheating so the chicken doesn’t clump together.

recipes.title: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir Fry
steps: You can use chicken broth in place of the chicken bouillon powder. Add 1/4 cup of broth followed by 2 teaspoons of cornstarch dissolved in 1 tablespoPrepare the tomatoes:
Slice the tomatoes in half. Remove the tough stem from each half that connects to the vine. Cut each half into equal thirds (you’ll get 6 slices from each tomato).
Make the soft scrambled eggs:

In a cold, 8 to 10-inch nonstick skillet, add the vegetable oil and beaten eggs. Turn the heat to medium. Once a thin layer of eggs is just beginning to cook on the bottom, push the eggs in one direction to create layers of scrambled eggs.
